<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="PartI"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">PART I</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="Business"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>Item 1.&#160;&#160;Business</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="General"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>GENERAL</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We are a multi-brand, specialty apparel retailer with a leading market share in women&#8217;s plus-size specialty apparel.&#160;&#160;During our fiscal year ended January 29, 2011 (&#8220;Fiscal 2010&#8221;) our business operations consisted primarily of three distinct core brands:&#160;&#160;LANE BRYANT<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font>, FASHION BUG<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font>, and CATHERINES PLUS SIZES<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font>.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#160;</font>These core brands operate retail stores and store-related e-commerce websites under our Retail Stores segment.&#160;&#160;Through our multiple channels, fashion content, and broad merchandise assortments, we seek to appeal to customers from a broad range of socioeconomic, demographic, and cultural groups.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 the sale of plus-size apparel represented approximately 82% of our total net sales.&#160;&#160;In addition to our Retail Stores segment we also derive revenues from sales of food and gifts through our FIGI&#8217;S<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font> catalog and website, which operate under our Direct-to-Consumer segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">LANE BRYANT</font> is a widely recognized brand name in plus-size fashion.&#160;&#160;Through private labels such as LANE BRYANT, CACIQUE<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font>, and select national brands, we offer fashionable and sophisticated apparel in plus-sizes 12&#160;&#8211; 32, including intimate apparel, wear-to-work and casual sportswear, accessories, select footwear, and social occasion apparel.&#160;&#160;LANE BRYANT has a loyal customer base, generally ranging in age from 35 to 55 years old, which shops for fashionable merchandise in the moderate price range.&#160;&#160;Our 731 LANE BRYANT retail stores comprise 4.3 million square feet of real estate and are located in 46 states and the District of Columbia, in a combination of destination malls, lifestyle centers, and strip shopping centers.&#160;&#160;Our average LANE BRYANT store size is approximately 5,900 square feet.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">lanebryant.com</font> website averaged 2.5 million unique visitors per month with an established on-line community.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our LANE BRYANT intimate apparel side-by-side store pairs LANE BRYANT&#8217;s casual and wear-to-work sportswear assortments with an expanded line of CACIQUE intimates as well as additional national brands, presented in a double store-front.&#160;&#160;This larger footprint of approximately 7,200 square feet per combined store compares with the full-line LANE BRYANT store average footprint of approximately 5,600 square feet.&#160;&#160;Included in the 731 stores operated by LANE BRYANT as of January 29, 2011 are 137 stores operated in the side-by-side format.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">LANE BRYANT OUTLET<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font> is a national chain offering women&#8217;s plus-size apparel in the outlet sales channel.&#160;&#160;Through our private labels and select national brands we offer fashionable and sophisticated apparel in plus-sizes 12&#160;&#8211; 32, including intimate apparel, wear-to-work and casual sportswear, accessories, select footwear, and social occasion apparel.&#160;&#160;Our 115 LANE BRYANT OUTLET retail stores comprise 0.7 million square feet of real estate and are located in 36 states throughout the country in outlet centers.&#160;&#160;Our average LANE BRYANT OUTLET store size is approximately 5,800 square feet.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">FASHION BUG</font> stores specialize in selling plus-size, misses, and junior apparel in sizes 6 &#8211; 30 serving women&#8217;s lifestyle needs from weekend to business wear, as well as accessories, intimate apparel, and footwear.&#160;&#160;FASHION BUG customers generally range in age from 30 to 50 years old and shop in the low-to-moderate price range.&#160;&#160;Our 743 FASHION BUG retail stores comprise 6.5 million square feet of real estate and are located in 43 states, primarily in strip shopping centers.&#160;&#160;Our average FASHION BUG store size is approximately 8,700 square feet.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">fashionbug.com</font> website averaged 1.5 million unique visitors per month.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CATHERINES PLUS SIZES</font> carries a full range of plus sizes (16&#160;&#8211; 34 and 0X&#160;&#8211; 5X) and is particularly known for extended sizes (28&#160;&#8211; 34).&#160;&#160;CATHERINES<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#174;</font> offers classic apparel and accessories for wear-to-work and casual lifestyles.&#160;&#160;CATHERINES customers are generally in the 45 years old and older age group, shop in the moderate price range, and are concerned with comfort, fit, and value.&#160;&#160;Our 475 CATHERINES retail stores comprise 1.9 million square feet of real estate and are located in 44 states, primarily in strip shopping centers.&#160;&#160;Our average CATHERINES store size is approximately 4,100 square feet.&#160;&#160;Included in the 475 stores operated by CATHERINES as of January 29, 2011 are 30 stores operated in outlet locations.&#160;&#160;Substantially all of the CATHERINES stores in outlet locations operate with a LANE BRYANT OUTLET store in side-by-side locations.&#160;&#160;These 30 stores average approximately 2,700 square feet, compared to the full-line CATHERINES stores average footprint of 4,200 square feet.&#160;&#160;In March 2011 we announced our plans to close the 30 CATHERINES stores in outlet locations (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations; OVERVIEW&#8221;</font> below).&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">catherines.com</font> website averaged more than 0.8 million unique visitors per month.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2010 we announced the debut of a universal shopping cart linking four of our e-commerce websites: <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">lanebryant.com</font>, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">cacique.com</font>, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">fashionbug.com</font>, and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">catherines.com</font>.&#160;&#160;We also began offering customer-friendly shipping options and added new search and navigation technology, making it easier for our customers to search our product offerings.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">FIGI&#8217;S markets food and specialty gift products through its FIGI&#8217;S Gifts in Good Taste catalog and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">figis.com</font> e-commerce website.&#160;&#160;FIGI&#8217;S specializes in dairy cheeses, smokehouse meats, holiday fare, bakery, chocolates, nuts, sweets, and snacks.&#160;&#160;FIGI&#8217;S also offers special gift assortments, collectibles, and exclusive and personalized items.&#160;&#160;FIGI&#8217;S Gallery offers home d&#233;cor, bedding, housewares, jewelry, garden accents, apparel, collectibles, gifts and other items through its catalog and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">figisgallery.com</font> e-commerce website.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 we expanded the sale of FIGI&#8217;S products into third-party retailers&#8217; stores and through third-party retailers&#8217; e-commerce websites.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Financial information by business segment for each of our last three fiscal years is included in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 18.&#160;&#160;SEGMENT REPORTING</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">See <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations; OVERVIEW&#8221; </font>below for further discussion of executive management changes during Fiscal 2010 and details regarding our management initiatives for Fiscal 2011.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our retail store merchandise displays enable our customers to assemble coordinated and complete outfits that satisfy their lifestyle needs.&#160;&#160;We test and implement new store designs and fixture packages that are aimed at providing an effective merchandise presentation.&#160;&#160;We relocate or remodel our stores as appropriate to convey a fresh and contemporary shopping environment.&#160;&#160;We emphasize customer service, including the presence of helpful salespeople in the stores, layaway plans, customer loyalty programs, and acceptance of merchandise returns for cash or credit within a reasonable time period.&#160;&#160;Typically, our stores are open seven days per week, eleven hours per day Monday through Saturday and seven hours on Sunday.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Retail stores operate under direct local management with guidance from our management operations team.&#160;&#160;Each store has a manager who is in daily operational control of and manages the specific location, including overseeing the duties of display, selling, and reporting through point-of-sale terminals.&#160;&#160;We employ district managers who regularly travel to all stores in their district to view store operations and provide guidance.&#160;&#160;Each district manager works with an average of 13 stores.&#160;&#160;Regional managers, who report to a Vice President of Stores, supervise the district managers.&#160;&#160;Generally, district managers are appointed from the pool of store managers and store managers are appointed from the pool of assistant store managers.&#160;&#160;Store management is motivated through internal advancement and promotion, competitive compensation, and various incentive, medical, and retirement plans.&#160;&#160;Store management also has access to centrally-developed resources on store operations, merchandising, and buying policies.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Merchandising and Buying</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We employ a brand-specific merchandising and buying strategy that is focused on providing an attractive selection of plus-size apparel and accessories that reflect the fashion preferences of the core customer for each of our retail store brands.&#160;&#160;We believe that the specialization of marketers and buyers within each brand enhances each brand&#8217;s identity and distinctiveness.&#160;&#160;We also use domestic and international fashion market guidance, fashion advisory services, and proprietary design.&#160;&#160;We seek to maintain high quality standards with respect to merchandise fabrication, construction, and fit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We continually refine our merchandise assortments to reflect the needs and demands of our diverse customer groups and the demographics of each store location.&#160;&#160;At LANE BRYANT we offer a combination of fashion basics and current fashions in casual and wear-to-work apparel, footwear, and accessories and our CACIQUE brand of intimate apparel, as well as other national brand sportswear and shapewear.&#160;&#160;We translate current trends into appropriate products for our customer.&#160;&#160;LANE BRYANT OUTLET features products developed exclusively for our outlet stores, which include updated key items and best-sellers from our full-line LANE BRYANT brand.&#160;&#160;Selected expanded categories, such as intimate apparel, footwear, social occasion, and accessories are also offered at LANE BRYANT OUTLET.&#160;&#160;At FASHION BUG we offer a broad assortment of weekend and business-wear apparel in plus, misses, junior, and junior plus sizes at low-to-moderate prices.&#160;&#160;FASHION BUG&#8217;s merchandise typically reflects established fashion trends and includes a broad offering of ready-to-wear apparel as well as footwear, accessories, intimate apparel, and seasonal items, such as swimwear and outerwear.&#160;&#160;At CATHERINES we offer a broad assortment of plus-size merchandise in classic styles designed to provide &#8220;head-to-toe&#8221; dressing for our customers.&#160;&#160;CATHERINES features casual and career sportswear, dresses, intimate apparel, suits, and accessories in a variety of plus-sizes, including petites and extended sizes.&#160;&#160;CATHERINES has developed a unique expertise in the comfort, fit, design, and manufacturing of extended sizes, making it one of the few retailers to emphasize these sizes.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We use our distribution capabilities to stock our stores with products specifically targeted to the store&#8217;s customer demographics.&#160;&#160;Our merchandising staff obtains store-wide and brand-wide inventory information generated by merchandise information systems that use our point-of-sale terminals.&#160;&#160;The status of our merchandise can be tracked from the placement of our initial order for the merchandise to the actual sale to our customer.&#160;&#160;Based on this data, our merchandise managers compare budgeted-to-actual sales and make merchandising decisions as needed, including re-order, markdowns, and changes in the buying plans for upcoming seasons.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our stores typically experience peak sales during the Easter, Labor Day, and December holiday seasons.&#160;&#160;We generally build inventory levels before these peak sales periods.&#160;&#160;To maintain current and fashionable inventory we reduce the price of slow-moving merchandise throughout the year.&#160;&#160;Much of our merchandise is developed for one or more of our four seasons: Spring, Summer, Fall, and Holiday.&#160;&#160;End-of-season sales are conducted with the objective of carrying an appropriate amount of seasonal merchandise over from one season to another.&#160;&#160;Retail Stores segment sales for the four quarters of Fiscal 2010, as a percent of annual Retail Stores segment sales, were 25.3%, 26.3%, 23.3%, and 25.1%, respectively.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Marketing and Promotions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We use several types of advertising to stimulate retail store customer traffic.&#160;&#160;We primarily use targeted direct-mail and e-mail advertising to preferred customers selected from a database of approximately 26.1 million private-label credit card, third-party credit card, and cash customers who have purchased merchandise from us within the past three years.&#160;&#160;We may also use radio, television, newspaper, internet advertising, fashion shows, social media, and other &#8220;grassroots&#8221; campaigns to stimulate traffic at certain strategic times of the year.&#160;&#160;We also use pricing policies, displays, store promotions, and convenient store hours and locations to attract customers.&#160;&#160;We maintain websites for our LANE BRYANT, FASHION BUG, and CATHERINES brands that provide information regarding current fashions and promotions and also provide internet shopping.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We offer our LANE BRYANT, FASHION BUG, and CATHERINES retail store customers various loyalty card programs.&#160;&#160;Customers who join these programs are entitled to various benefits, including discounts on purchases, during the membership period.&#160;&#160;Customers join some of these programs by paying an annual membership fee.&#160;&#160;Other programs are offered that do not require the payment of a membership fee but allow cardholders to earn points for purchases using a private-label credit card, which may be redeemed for merchandise coupons upon the accumulation of a specified number of points.&#160;&#160;Additional information on our loyalty card programs is included in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CRITICAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">; </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loyalty Card Programs</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Sourcing</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">To meet the demands of our customers we access both the overseas and domestic wholesale markets for our Retail Stores segment merchandise purchases.&#160;&#160;We primarily source from outside of the United States and source merchandise both through our overseas sourcing operation, where we are the importer of record, and from domestic vendors that also source merchandise from overseas.&#160;&#160;This allows us to maintain flexible lead times, respond quickly to current fashion trends, and replenish merchandise inventory as necessary.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 we purchased merchandise from approximately 390 suppliers located throughout the world.&#160;&#160;We also purchase a portion of our LANE BRYANT merchandise from Mast Industries, Inc. (&#8220;Mast&#8221;), a contract manufacturer and apparel importer that is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Limited Brands, Inc.&#160;&#160;These purchases from Mast accounted for approximately 7% of our total Retail Stores merchandise purchases and approximately 15% of merchandise purchases for LANE BRYANT and LANE BRYANT OUTLET during Fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;No other vendor accounted for more than 3% of total Retail Stores segment merchandise purchases during Fiscal 2010.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We pay for a majority of our merchandise purchases outside the United States on an open account basis.&#160;&#160;We pay for the remainder of our purchases outside the United States primarily through corporate-issued letters of credit where we are the importer of record.&#160;&#160;The geographic diversification of our sourcing network provides us with the flexibility to locate alternate sources for our products in order to meet our pricing targets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">To date, we have not experienced difficulties in purchasing merchandise overseas or importing such merchandise into the United States.&#160;&#160;Should events such as political instability or a natural disaster result in a disruption of normal activities in any single country with which we do business, we believe that we would have adequate alternative sources of supply.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Distribution and Logistics</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We currently operate two distribution centers for our Retail Stores segment.&#160;&#160;For our FASHION BUG and LANE BRYANT OUTLET stores we operate a distribution center in Greencastle, Indiana.&#160;&#160;This facility is located on a 126-acre tract of land and contains a building of approximately 865,000 square feet.&#160;&#160;We estimate that this facility has the capacity to service up to approximately 1,800 stores.&#160;&#160;For our LANE BRYANT and CATHERINES stores we operate a distribution center in White Marsh, Maryland.&#160;&#160;The White Marsh facility is located on 28 acres of land and contains a building of approximately 513,000 square feet that is currently designed to service up to approximately 1,600 stores.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The vast majority of our merchandise purchases are received at these distribution facilities, where they are prepared for distribution to our stores.&#160;&#160;Automated sorting systems in the distribution centers enhance the flow of merchandise from receipt to quality control inspection, receiving, ticketing, packing, and final shipment.&#160;&#160;Merchandise is shipped to each store principally by common carriers.&#160;&#160;We use computerized automated distribution attributes to combine shipments when possible and improve the efficiency of the distribution operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Inventory and fulfillment activities for our store-related e-commerce operations are handled by a third-party warehouse facility in Indianapolis, Indiana, using approximately 310,000 square feet of space for merchandise receipt, storage, picking, packing, shipping, and returns processing.&#160;&#160;Approximately half of the merchandise received by this third-party facility is shipped from our Greencastle and White Marsh distribution centers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our distribution and logistics operations provide adequate capacity for the foreseeable future, and we continually evaluate our overall long-term distribution and logistics requirements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="DirectToConsumerSegment"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>DIRECT-TO-CONSUMER SEGMENT</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Direct-to-Consumer segment consists primarily of the operations of our FIGI&#8217;S business, which markets food and specialty gift products through our FIGI&#8217;S Gifts in Good Taste catalog and related e-commerce website.&#160;&#160;FIGI&#8217;S experiences a peak sales period during the December holiday season, with approximately 76% of its annual sales occurring during our fourth quarter.&#160;&#160;FIGI&#8217;S offers interest-free, three-payment credit terms over three months to its customers, with the first payment due on a defined date 30 to 60 days after a stated holiday.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 we expanded the sale of FIGI&#8217;S products into third-party retailers&#8217; stores and through third-party retailers&#8217; e-commerce websites.&#160;&#160;We also operate FIGI&#8217;S Gallery, which offers home d&#233;cor, bedding, housewares, jewelry, garden accents, apparel, collectibles, gifts, and other items through its catalog and e-commerce website.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">COMPETITION</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The women's specialty retail apparel business is highly competitive, with numerous competitors, including individual and chain fashion specialty stores, department stores, discount stores, catalog retailers, and internet-based retailers, some of which may have greater financial resources, marketing capabilities, or brand recognition than we have.&#160;&#160;We cannot reasonably estimate the number of our competitors due to the large number of women&#8217;s apparel retailers.&#160;&#160;The primary elements of competition are merchandise style, size, selection, fit, quality, display, price, attractive website layout, efficient fulfillment of website mail orders, and personalized service to our customers.&#160;&#160;For our retail stores, store location, design, advertising, and promotion are also significant elements of competition.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">RISKS RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS AND INDUSTRY</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Ongoing economic conditions have adversely affected, and may continue to adversely affect, our business and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Consumer spending habits, including spending for our products, are affected by, among other things, prevailing economic conditions, levels of employment, salary levels, wage rates, availability of consumer credit, consumer confidence, fluctuating fuel and energy costs, and consumer perception of economic conditions.&#160;&#160;Consumer discretionary spending, including purchases of women&#8217;s apparel, tends to decline during periods of high unemployment, which can have an adverse impact on our results of operations.&#160;&#160;We could be required to take additional markdowns in response to lower-than-anticipated levels of demand for our products, and promotional activity by our competitors could have a further adverse impact on our results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We cannot reliably predict the extent to which current or future economic conditions will affect our business.&#160;&#160;A prolonged continuation of reduced consumer demand for our products could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our business is dependent upon our ability to accurately predict rapidly changing fashion trends, customer preferences, and other fashion-related factors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Customer tastes and fashion trends are volatile and tend to change rapidly, particularly for women's apparel.&#160;&#160;Our success depends in part on our ability to effectively predict and respond to quickly changing fashion tastes and consumer demands, and to translate market trends into appropriate, saleable product offerings.&#160;&#160;These risks may increase as we shift a higher proportion of our product from third-party vendors and domestic sourcing to internally-designed merchandise and overseas sourcing.&#160;&#160;The increased lead times associated with overseas sourcing could increase our risk of misjudging fashion trends or styles.&#160;&#160;If we are unable to successfully predict or respond to changing styles or trends and misjudge the market for our products or any new product lines, our sales will be lower and we may be faced with a substantial amount of unsold inventory or missed sales opportunities.&#160;&#160;In response, we may be forced to rely on additional markdowns or promotional sales to dispose of excess or slow-moving inventory, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.&#160;&#160;This could also impact our reputation with our customers, which could diminish brand loyalty.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Existing and increased competition in the women's retail apparel and direct-to-consumer markets may reduce our net revenues, profits, and market share.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The women&#8217;s specialty retail apparel and direct-to-consumer markets are highly competitive.&#160;&#160;Our competitors include individual and chain fashion specialty stores, department stores, discount stores, catalog retailers, and internet-based retailers.&#160;&#160;As a result of this competition we are required to effectively market and competitively price our products to consumers in diverse markets, and we typically experience pricing pressures, which may require us to incur increased marketing expenditures, and could lead to loss of market share.&#160;&#160;Existing and increased competition could result in reduced sales and margins, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We believe that the principal bases upon which we compete are merchandise style, size, selection, fit, quality, display, price, attractive website layout, efficient fulfillment of website mail orders, and personalized service to our customers, as well as store location, design, advertising, and promotion.&#160;&#160;Other women&#8217;s apparel and direct-to-consumer companies with greater financial resources, marketing capabilities, or brand recognition may enter the plus-size business and may be able to devote greater resources to the marketing and sale of their products, implement more aggressive pricing policies, introduce new products more quickly, and respond and adapt to future economic downturns more effectively.&#160;&#160;We cannot give assurance that we will be able to compete successfully against existing or future competitors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our business plan is largely dependent upon continued growth in the plus-size women&#8217;s apparel market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our business is primarily focused on sales of plus-size women&#8217;s apparel, which represents a majority of our total net sales.&#160;&#160;Our results of operations could be adversely affected by a lack of continued growth in the plus-size women&#8217;s apparel market.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We depend on key personnel and may not be able to retain or replace these employees or recruit additional qualified personnel.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our success and our ability to execute our business strategy depend largely on the efforts and abilities of our executive officers and our management teams and our ability to attract, hire, and retain officers and management.&#160;&#160;We also must motivate employees to remain focused on our strategies and goals, particularly during a period of changing executive leadership at both our corporate level and our operating division level.&#160;&#160;If we cannot hire and retain effective management, we may be unable to compete effectively with other retailers.&#160;&#160;We do not maintain key-person life insurance policies with respect to any of our employees.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We may be unable to successfully execute on our business plans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We cannot assure the successful execution and the realization of the benefits of our business plans, which may vary materially based on various factors.&#160;&#160;Recent additions to our management and our effort to improve our competitive position and results of operations are based on certain assumptions that may prove to be inaccurate.&#160;&#160;Our&#160;business plans&#160;are subject to numerous risks and uncertainties that may change over time, and we may not achieve the desired results.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Improving our operating margins is dependent on our ability to successfully control our operating costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In order to improve our operating margins we need to successfully manage our operating costs.&#160;&#160;Our inability to successfully manage labor costs, occupancy costs, transportation costs, or other operating costs, or our inability to take advantage of opportunities to reduce operating costs, could decrease our operating margins and could adversely affect our results of operations.&#160;&#160;In addition, we may be unable to obtain adequate insurance coverage for our operations at a reasonable cost.&#160;&#160;We cannot assure the successful implementation of our turnaround programs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Certain key raw materials in our products, such as cotton, wool, and synthetic fabrics, are subject to availability constraints and price volatility.&#160;&#160;An increase in the cost or decrease in the availability of such raw materials could adversely affect our operating margins and our results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We are subject to the Fair Labor Standards Act and various state and Federal laws and regulations governing such matters as minimum wages, exempt status classification, overtime, and employee benefits.&#160;&#160;Changes in Federal or state laws or regulations regarding minimum wages, unionization, or other employee benefits could cause us to incur additional wage and benefit costs, which could adversely affect our results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We may not be able to obtain sufficient working capital financing on terms acceptable to us.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our business requires substantial investment in our inventory for several months before sales of that inventory occur.&#160;&#160;Consequently, we require significant amounts of working capital financing.&#160;&#160;We depend on the availability of credit to fund our working capital, including credit we receive from our bankers, our factors, our suppliers and their agents, and on our ongoing payments from our strategic alliance related to private-label credit card sales.&#160;&#160;If we or our vendors are unable to obtain sufficient financing at an affordable cost, our ability to merchandise our retail stores or e-commerce businesses could be adversely affected.</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We cannot assure that we will realize the expected benefits from our private-label credit card programs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We cannot assure that we will realize the expected benefits from the private-label credit card operating agreements with Alliance Data.&#160;&#160;A significant portion of our sales revenues is generated through our private-label credit cards.&#160;&#160;Therefore, changes in the private-label credit card programs that adversely impact our ability to facilitate customer credit may adversely impact our results of operations.&#160;&#160;Alliance Data has discretion over certain policies and arrangements with the cardholders and may change these policies and arrangements in ways that could affect our relationship with the cardholders.&#160;&#160;Any such changes could adversely affect our private-label credit card sales and our results of operations.&#160;&#160;Our ability to continue to offer private-label credit card programs to our customers will depend on the success of our strategic alliance with Alliance Data.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Credit card operations are subject to numerous Federal and state laws, including, in particular, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act signed into law on July 21, 2010, that impose disclosure and other requirements upon the origination, servicing, and enforcement of credit accounts, and limitations on the amount of finance charges and fees that may be charged by a credit card provider.&#160;&#160;Alliance Data may be subject to regulations to which we were not subject prior to the sale of the proprietary credit card receivables programs.&#160;&#160;To the extent that such limitations or regulations materially limit the availability of credit or increase the cost of credit to our cardholders or negatively impact provisions which affect our revenue streams associated with the private-label credit card operating agreements, our results of operations could be adversely affected.&#160;&#160;In addition, changes in credit card use, payment patterns, or default rates could be affected by a variety of economic, legal, social, or other factors over which we have no control and cannot predict with certainty.&#160;&#160;Such changes could also negatively impact the availability of credit or increase the cost of credit to our cardholders or negatively impact provisions that affect our revenue streams associated with the operating agreements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our operating results fluctuate from season to season.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our retail store and direct-to-consumer operations experience seasonal fluctuations in net sales and consequently in operating income, with peak sales typically occurring during the Easter, Labor Day, and December holiday seasons for our Retail Stores segment and in the December holiday season for our Direct-to-Consumer segment.&#160;&#160;In addition, extreme or unseasonable weather can affect our sales.&#160;&#160;Any decrease in net sales or margins during our peak selling periods, or in the availability of working capital needed in the months before these periods, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We usually order merchandise in advance of peak selling periods and sometimes before new fashion trends are confirmed by customer purchases.&#160;&#160;We must carry a significant amount of inventory, including perishable products for our FIGI&#8217;S food and gifts operations, before the peak selling periods.&#160;&#160;If we are not successful in selling our inventory, especially during our peak selling periods, we may be forced to rely on markdowns or promotional sales to dispose of the inventory or we may not be able to sell the inventory at all, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our operating results are dependent in part on our ability to effectively manage our inventory levels.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We must maintain the right mix and level of inventory to operate our business successfully.&#160;&#160;Excess inventory creates pricing pressures, while insufficient inventory could lead to decreased sales and a loss of customers.&#160;&#160;We continually evaluate the market and the mood of our customers to determine our optimal inventory levels.&#160;&#160;If we do not correctly anticipate the demand for one or more of our products or delay placing seasonal inventory in our stores for too long, our results of operations and business could be adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Certain of our business processes that are dependent on technology are outsourced.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Certain of our business processes that are dependent on technology are outsourced to third parties.&#160;&#160;Such processes include payroll processing, credit card authorization and processing, our e-commerce platform, and certain other information technology functions.&#160;&#160;Although we make a diligent effort to ensure that all providers of outsourced services observe proper internal control practices and procedures, we cannot assure that failures will not occur.&#160;&#160;The failure of such third parties to provide adequate services could adversely affect our customers&#8217; shopping experience, our results of operations, liquidity, or our ability to provide adequate financial and management reporting.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We could be materially and adversely affected if any of our distribution or fulfillment centers are shut down.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We operate distribution and fulfillment centers in Greencastle, Indiana; White Marsh, Maryland; Marshfield, Wisconsin; Stevens Point, Wisconsin; and Neillsville, Wisconsin and use a third-party fulfillment center in Indianapolis, Indiana that services our e-commerce operations.&#160;&#160;In addition, we use third-party freight consolidators and service providers in Los Angeles, California and North Bergen, New Jersey.&#160;&#160;Most of the merchandise we purchase is shipped either directly or via freight consolidators to our distribution and fulfillment centers.&#160;&#160;If any of our distribution centers, fulfillment centers, or freight consolidators were to shut down or lose significant capacity for any reason, the other locations may not be able to adequately support the resulting additional distribution demands, in part because of capacity constraints and in part because not all brands are supported at each location.&#160;&#160;As a result, we could incur significantly higher costs and experience longer lead times associated with distributing our products to our stores or customers during the time it takes for us to reopen or replace the affected distribution center, fulfillment center, or freight consolidator.&#160;&#160;Should the third-party fulfillment center that services our e-commerce operations cease providing fulfillment services the resultant failure to deliver e-commerce orders promptly could adversely affect our e-commerce operations and our results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Natural disasters, war, acts of terrorism, or other armed conflict may negatively impact the availability of merchandise and otherwise adversely impact our business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The occurrence of, or threat of, a natural disaster, war, acts of terrorism, or other armed conflict on the United States or international economies could negatively affect our ability to obtain merchandise for sale.&#160;&#160;A significant portion of our merchandise is imported from other countries.&#160;&#160;If imported goods become difficult or impossible to bring into the United States and we cannot obtain such merchandise from other sources at similar costs, our net sales and profit margins may be adversely impacted.&#160;&#160;If commercial transportation is curtailed or substantially delayed our business may be adversely impacted, as we may have difficulty shipping merchandise to our distribution centers, fulfillment centers, freight consolidators, stores, or our direct-to-consumer customers.&#160;&#160;As a result of the occurrence of, or threat of, a natural disaster or acts of terrorism in the United States we may be required to suspend operations in some or all of our stores, which could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our inability to successfully manage customer service or fulfillment for our e-commerce websites could adversely impact our results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Successful operation of our e-commerce websites and our catalog business is dependent on our ability to maintain efficient and uninterrupted customer service and fulfillment operations.&#160;&#160;Inadequate systems capacity, a disruption or slowdown in telecommunications services, changes in technology, changes in government regulations, systems issues, security breaches, or customer privacy issues could result in reduced sales or increases in operating expenses as a result of our efforts or our inability to remedy such issues.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our purchasing patterns are dictated by our seasonal inventory requirements.&#160;&#160;We typically enter into purchase commitments with our vendors for seasonal inventories up to six months ahead of when we take delivery of those products.&#160;&#160;All of our purchase commitments with foreign vendors are denominated in U.S. dollars and are settled in U.S. dollars.&#160;&#160;These arrangements provide a natural hedge to the impacts of changes in the value of the U.S. dollar relative to the foreign currencies during the period from when we enter into purchase commitments with our vendors to when we take delivery of the products in the countries from which we source our products.&#160;&#160;However, changes in the value of the U.S. dollar relative to other currencies can impact the negotiated pricing for products when comparing one seasonal buying period to another.&#160;&#160;We have a network of countries and vendors from which we can source, but a weakening of the U.S. dollar in relation to those foreign currencies could increase the cost of our foreign-sourced products.&#160;&#160;The future performance of our business depends on our foreign suppliers and may be adversely affected by the factors listed above, which are beyond our control.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Issues of global workplace conditions may adversely affect our business.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -5.75pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">If any one of our manufacturers or vendors fails to operate in compliance with applicable laws and regulations, is perceived by the public as failing to meet certain United States labor standards, or employs unfair labor practices, our business could be adversely affected.&#160;&#160;Current global workplace concerns of the public include wages, working conditions, age of employees, and various other employment standards.&#160;&#160;These globalization issues may affect the available supply of certain manufacturers' products, which may result in increased costs to us.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, a negative customer perception of any of our key vendors or their products may result in a lower customer demand for our apparel.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our sales are dependent in part on a high volume of strip shopping center and mall traffic.&#160;&#160;Strip shopping center and mall traffic may be adversely affected by, among other things, economic downturns, the closing of anchor stores, or changes in customer shopping preferences.&#160;&#160;A decline in the popularity of strip shopping center or mall shopping among our target customers could have a material adverse effect on our business.&#160;&#160;To take advantage of customer traffic and the shopping preferences of our customers we need to maintain or acquire stores in desirable locations.&#160;&#160;We cannot assure that desirable store locations will continue to be available.&#160;&#160;In addition, the timely opening of new store locations could be adversely affected by delays in obtaining necessary permits and approvals, lack of availability of construction materials and labor, or work stoppages.&#160;&#160;Our ability to acquire or maintain desirable store locations could be adversely affected by financial difficulties encountered by strip shopping center or mall landlords or by competition with other retailers for prime locations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><a name="LegalProceedings"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Item 3.&#160;&#160;Legal Proceedings</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In August 2009, Sharon Bates and Tamara Baggett, former Store Sales Managers (&#8220;SSMs&#8221;) of stores under the trade name &#8220;Catherines,&#8221; filed a Complaint with the United States District Court, District of Connecticut, against Catherines, Inc. (&#8220;Catherines&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The complaint, as amended, alleges that the plaintiffs were unlawfully denied overtime compensation.&#160;&#160;Ms. Bates' individual overtime claim was brought under the Connecticut Minimum Wage Act (&#8220;CMWA&#8221;) and Ms. Baggett's individual overtime claim was brought under the New York Minimum Wage Act (&#8220;NYMWA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;In addition, both Plaintiffs asserted claims on behalf of themselves and other purportedly similarly-situated current and former SSMs under the Fair Labor Standards Act (&#8220;FLSA&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Plaintiffs seek unpaid overtime wages, liquidated damages, interest and costs, attorneys&#8217; fees, an order enjoining Catherines from continuing its alleged illegal practices in violation of the FLSA, NYMWA and CMWA as to current and future SSMs, and such other relief as the Court deems equitable.&#160;&#160;Catherines has filed its Answer to the Amended Complaint denying Plaintiffs&#8217; allegations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; DISPLAY: inline">On or about May 27, 2010, Plaintiffs filed a Motion to Proceed as a Collective Action with the United States District Court, District of Connecticut.&#160;&#160;In that motion, Plaintiffs seek approval from the Court to send notice of the lawsuit to purportedly similarly-situated current and former SSMs working with Catherines after August 18, 2006, who may, after receiving the notice, elect to participate in the lawsuit as plaintiffs.&#160;&#160;Catherines is opposing this motion, and oral argument was heard on the motion on August 20, 2010.&#160;&#160;If the motion is granted, the scope of the litigation may expand significantly.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt"><font style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; DISPLAY: inline">In addition, Catherines has filed a Summary Judgment Motion to dismiss the claims of Plaintiff Bates.&#160;&#160;Plaintiffs' opposition to the motion was filed and the Court heard oral argument on the motion. </font><font style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font><font style="BACKGROUND-COLOR: #ffffff; DISPLAY: inline">To date, the court has not ruled on the two motions before it and the parties are engaged in settlement negotiations through the use of an independent mediator.&#160;&#160;As a result of such negotiations, the parties have reached a tentative agreement and are in the process of finalizing the terms of a settlement proposal to be presented to the court for approval.&#160;&#160;Any settlement of the dispute will require final court approval.</font>&#160;&#160;The terms of the settlement proposal would not have a material impact on our financial condition or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have not paid any dividends since 1995, and we do not expect to declare or pay any dividends on our common stock in the foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;The payment of future dividends is within the discretion of our Board of Directors and will depend upon our future earnings, if any, our capital requirements, our financial condition, and other relevant factors.&#160;&#160;Our revolving credit facility allows the payment of dividends on our common stock not to exceed $15 million in any fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Such payments are subject to maintaining a minimum level of &#8220;Excess Availability&#8221; (as defined in the facility agreement) for 30 days before the payment of such dividends, immediately after the payment of such dividends, and on a projected pro-forma basis for 12 consecutive fiscal months thereafter.&#160;&#160;(See <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Item 7.&#160;&#160;Management&#8217;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">FINANCIAL CONDITION</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">; Financing; </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revolving Credit Facility</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Item 8.&#160;&#160;Financial Statements and Supplementary Data; Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements; </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 7.&#160;&#160;LONG-TERM DEBT</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> below).</font></div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenue Recognition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our revenues from merchandise sales are net of sales discounts, returns, and allowances and exclude sales tax.&#160;&#160;We record a reserve for estimated future sales returns based on an analysis of actual returns and we defer recognition of layaway sales to the date of delivery.&#160;&#160;A change in our actual rates of sales returns and layaway sales experience would affect the level of revenue recognized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Catalog and e-commerce revenues include shipping and handling fees billed to customers.&#160;&#160;These revenues are recognized after all of the following have occurred: execution of the customer&#8217;s order, authorization of the customer&#8217;s credit card has been received, and the product has been shipped to and received by the customer.&#160;&#160;We defer recognition of revenue for product shipped but not yet received by the customer based on an estimate of the number of days the shipments are in-transit.&#160;&#160;A change in the time it takes for customers to receive our products would affect the level of revenue recognized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We sell gift cards to our Retail Stores segment customers through our stores, store-related websites, and through third parties.&#160;&#160;We recognize revenue from gift cards when the gift card is redeemed by the customer.&#160;&#160;Our gift cards do not contain expiration dates or inactivity fees.&#160;&#160;We recognize gift card breakage (unused gift card balances for which we believe the likelihood of redemption is remote) as net sales based on an analysis of historical redemption patterns.&#160;&#160;A change in the historical pattern of gift card redemptions would affect the level of revenue recognized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loyalty Card Programs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We offer our customers various loyalty card programs.&#160;&#160;Customers that join these programs are entitled to various benefits, including discounts on purchases, during the membership period.&#160;&#160;Customers join some of these programs by paying an annual membership fee.&#160;&#160;For these programs we recognize revenue as a component of net sales over the life of the membership period based on when the customer earns the benefits and when the fee is no longer refundable.&#160;&#160;Certain loyalty card customers earn points for purchases which may be redeemed for merchandise coupons upon the accumulation of a specified number of points.&#160;&#160;No membership fees are charged in connection with these programs.&#160;&#160;We recognize an accrual for discounts earned and not yet issued and discounts issued but not yet redeemed based on an analysis of historical redemption patterns.&#160;&#160;Costs we incur in connection with administering these programs are recognized in selling, general, and administrative expenses as incurred.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounts Receivable</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our FIGI&#8217;S food and gifts business offers credit to its customers using interest-free three-payment credit terms over three months, with the first payment due on a defined date 30 to 60 days after a stated holiday.&#160;&#160;A substantial portion of the FIGI&#8217;S business is conducted during the December holiday season.&#160;&#160;We evaluate the collectibility of our accounts receivable based on a combination of factors, including analysis of historical trends, aging of accounts receivable, write-off experience, past history of recoveries, and expectations of future performance.&#160;&#160;Significant changes in future performance relative to our historical experience could have an impact on the levels of our accounts receivable valuation reserves.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt"><a href="#TableofContents">Table of Contents</a></font></div>
