</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="NotestoFinStmts"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>NOTE 1.&#160;&#160;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fiscal Year</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have a 52<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">-</font>53 week fiscal year ending on the Saturday nearest to January 31.&#160;&#160;A 52-week fiscal year consists of four 13-week quarters and a 53-week period consists of three 13-week quarters and a 14-week fourth quarter.&#160;&#160;As used herein, the terms &#8220;Fiscal 2010,&#8221; &#8220;Fiscal 2009,&#8221; and &#8220;Fiscal 2008,&#8221; refer to our fiscal years ended January 29, 2011, January 30, 2010, and January 31, 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We operate retail specialty stores located throughout the continental United States and related websites that merchandise plus-size, junior, and misses sportswear, dresses, coats, and intimate apparel, as well as accessories and casual footwear, at a wide range of prices.&#160;&#160;We also conduct a direct marketing operation that merchandises food and specialty gifts throughout the continental United States through our FIGI&#8217;S Gifts in Good Taste catalog and related website.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2009 we discontinued our LANE BRYANT WOMAN catalog.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2008 we began to explore strategic alternatives for our Crosstown Traders non-core misses apparel catalog titles in order to provide a greater focus on our core brands and enhance shareholder value.&#160;&#160;We completed the sale of the Crosstown Traders apparel catalog operations in September 2008 and accounted for the operations of the Crosstown Traders apparel catalogs as discontinued operations (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS&#8221;</font> below).&#160;&#160;Except as otherwise indicated, the financial information included in these Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements reflects only the results of our continuing operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Principles of Consolidation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The consolidated financial statements include the accounts of Charming Shoppes, Inc. and our wholly-owned and majority-owned subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;All inter-company accounts and transactions have been eliminated.&#160;&#160;The terms &#8220;the Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us,&#8221; and &#8220;our&#8221; refer to Charming Shoppes, Inc., and, where applicable, our consolidated subsidiaries.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Business Segments and Related Disclosures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We operate in two segments, Retail Stores and Direct-to-Consumer.&#160;&#160;We determine our operating segments based on the way our chief operating decision-makers review our results of operations.&#160;&#160;We consider our retail stores and store-related e-commerce as operating segments that are similar in terms of economic characteristics, production processes, and operations.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we have aggregated our retail stores and store-related e-commerce into a single reporting segment (the &#8220;Retail Stores&#8221; segment).&#160;&#160;Our catalog and catalog-related e-commerce operations are separately reported under the Direct-to-Consumer segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Retail Stores segment derives its revenues from sales through retail stores and store-related e-commerce sales under our LANE BRYANT<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top">&#160;</font>(including LANE BRYANT OUTLET)<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">, </font>FASHION BUG, and CATHERINES PLUS SIZES brands, and previously our PETITE SOPHISTICATE OUTLET brand, which was discontinued during Fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;The Direct-to-Consumer segment derives its revenues from catalog sales and catalog-related e-commerce sales under our FIGI&#8217;S title, and previously our LANE BRYANT WOMAN title, which was discontinued during Fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;Our foreign sourcing operations do not constitute a material geographic segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2009 we completed the sale of our proprietary credit card receivables programs (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 11.&#160;&#160;SALE OF PROPRIETARY CREDIT CARD RECEIVABLES PROGRAMS</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> below).&#160;&#160;As a result of the sale, we began to allocate the operating results of our credit card operations, including revenue from our customer loyalty programs, to the Retail Stores segment.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we have restated the results of the Retail Stores and Corporate and Other segments for Fiscal 2009 and Fiscal 2008 to reflect this change in how our chief operating decision-makers evaluate the performance of our operating segments.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">See <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 18.&#160;&#160;SEGMENT REPORTING</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> below for further information regarding our operations by business segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Foreign Operations</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We use a December 31 fiscal year for our foreign subsidiaries in order to expedite our year-end closing.&#160;&#160;There were no intervening events or transactions with respect to our foreign subsidiaries during the period from January 1, 2011 to January 29, 2011 that would have a material effect on our financial position or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Use of Estimates</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The preparation of financial statements in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles requires that our management make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and accompanying notes.&#160;&#160;Actual results could differ from those estimates.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Reclassifications</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Certain prior-year amounts related to deferred tax assets and liabilities have been reclassified to conform to the current-year presentation.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cash Equivalents</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We consider all highly-liquid investments with a maturity of three months or less when purchased to be cash equivalents.&#160;&#160;These amounts are stated at cost, which approximates market value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Accounts Receivable</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our FIGI&#8217;S food and gifts business offers credit to its customers using interest-free, three-payment credit terms over three months, with the first payment due on a defined date 30 to 60 days after a stated holiday.&#160;&#160;A substantial portion of the FIGI&#8217;S business is conducted during the December holiday season.&#160;&#160;We evaluate the collectibility of our accounts receivable based on a combination of factors, including analysis of historical trends, aging of accounts receivable, write-off experience, past history of recoveries, and expectations of future performance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Inventories</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We value merchandise inventories for our Retail Stores and Direct-to-Consumer segments at the lower of cost or market using the retail inventory method (average cost basis).&#160;&#160;Under the retail inventory method the valuation of inventories at cost and the resulting gross margins are adjusted in proportion to markdowns currently taken and shrinkage on the retail value of inventories.&#160;&#160;In addition to markdowns that have been taken (i.e., selling price permanently reduced on the selling floor) we accrue an estimate for promotional markdowns not yet recorded for seasonal merchandise that will not be sold again above its current promotional price.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We purchase inventory and track inventory quantities on hand by season in order to determine aged seasonal inventory.&#160;&#160;We liquidate aged seasonal inventory through markdowns or sale to liquidators.&#160;&#160;We account for store inventory shrinkage based on physical inventories conducted at least once annually on a store-by-store basis, with supplemental observations in locations exhibiting high shrinkage rates.&#160;&#160;We account for distribution and fulfillment center inventory shrinkage based on cycle counts on a center-by-center basis.&#160;&#160;Actual inventory losses are recorded in our financial statements at the time these physical inventory observations are performed.&#160;&#160;We determine interim shrinkage estimates based on the actual inventory losses identified by the physical inventory counts at our stores and distribution centers and record a reserve for estimated inventory losses (shrinkage).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We record cash consideration received from vendors as a reduction of inventory and recognize it in cost of goods sold as inventory is sold.&#160;&#160;We defer the recognition of cash received from vendors during interim periods in order to better match the recognition of the cash consideration to the period the inventory is sold.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Prepayments and Other</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Prepayments and other includes prepaid taxes, insurance, rent, marketing, deferred advertising costs, and other prepaid expenses.&#160;&#160;Prepayments and other also includes third-party credit card receivables and income taxes receivable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deferred and Non-Deferred Advertising Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">With the exception of direct-response advertising, we expense advertising costs when the related advertising takes place.&#160;&#160;We capitalize all direct costs incurred in the development, production, and circulation of our direct-mail catalogs until the related catalog is mailed.&#160;&#160;These capitalized costs are amortized as a component of cost of goods sold over the expected sales realization cycle of the catalog, which is generally within one to six months.&#160;&#160;Beginning in Fiscal 2009, advertising costs are net of restricted and unrestricted marketing expense reimbursements we receive under our operating agreements related to the sale of our proprietary credit card receivables programs (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 11. SALE OF PROPRIETARY CREDIT CARD RECEIVABLES PROGRAMS&#8221;</font> below).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Property and Depreciation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For financial reporting purposes we compute depreciation and amortization primarily using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets.&#160;&#160;We amortize leasehold improvements over the shorter of their useful lives or the related lease term as determined under our operating lease accounting policy (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Lease Accounting&#8221;</font> below).&#160;&#160;We use accelerated depreciation methods for income tax reporting purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We assess our long-lived assets for recoverability whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amounts of long-lived assets may not be recoverable.&#160;&#160;We consider historical performance and future estimated results when evaluating an asset for potential impairment, and we compare the carrying amount of the asset to the estimated future undiscounted cash flows expected to result from the use of the asset.&#160;&#160;If the estimated future undiscounted cash flows are less than the carrying amount of the asset, we write down the asset to its estimated fair value and recognize an impairment loss.&#160;&#160;Our estimate of fair value is generally based on either appraised value or the present value of future cash flows and is a &#8220;Level 3&#8221; fair value measurement (based on unobservable inputs that are not corroborated by market data).&#160;&#160;The estimates and assumptions that we use to evaluate possible impairment require certain significant assumptions regarding factors such as future sales growth and operating performance, and they may change as new events occur or as additional information is obtained.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">See <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 12. IMPAIRMENT OF STORE ASSETS, GOODWILL, AND TRADEMARKS&#8221;</font> below for further details regarding the recognition of impairment losses related to our long-lived assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Lease Accounting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We lease substantially all of our store properties as well as certain of our other facilities and account for these leases as operating leases.&#160;&#160;A majority of our store leases contain lease options that we can unilaterally exercise.&#160;&#160;The lease term we use for such leases includes lease option renewal periods only in instances in which the failure to exercise such options would result in an economic penalty for us and exercise of the renewal option is therefore reasonably assured at the lease inception date.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For leases that contain rent escalations, the lease term for recognition of straight-line rent expense commences on the date we take possession of the leased property for construction purposes, which for stores is generally two months prior to a store opening date.&#160;&#160;Similarly, landlord incentives or allowances under operating leases (tenant improvement allowances) are recorded as a deferred rent liability.&#160;&#160;The deferred rent liability is amortized as a reduction of rent expense on a straight-line basis over the lease term, commencing on the date we take possession of the leased property for construction purposes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Contingent rent is determined on a store-by-store basis based on criteria set forth in the lease.&#160;&#160;Generally, a landlord is due incremental rent when a store exceeds a sales threshold that is determined in the lease.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Goodwill and Other Intangible Assets</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We own trademarks, tradenames, and internet domain names that we obtained primarily from our acquisition of LANE BRYANT.&#160;&#160;We also own trademarks, tradenames, internet domain names, and customer relationships for our FIGI&#8217;S catalog and related website.&#160;&#160;In addition, we previously owned such assets in connection with our acquisition of Crosstown Traders (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS&#8221;</font> below).&#160;&#160;The values of these intangible assets were determined by management with the assistance of an independent appraiser using a discounted cash flow method, based on the estimated future benefits to be received from the assets.&#160;&#160;We allocated the excess of the cost of the acquisitions over the estimated fair value of the identifiable tangible and intangible net assets acquired to goodwill.&#160;&#160;We amortize separate intangible assets that are not deemed to have an indefinite life on a straight-line basis over their useful lives.&#160;&#160;We do not amortize goodwill.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our LANE BRYANT, FIGI&#8217;S, and other trademarks, tradenames, and internet domain names are well-recognized in the marketplace, and we expect to renew and protect these assets indefinitely.&#160;&#160;Therefore, we are not amortizing the appraised value of these trademarks, tradenames, and internet domain names.&#160;&#160;We periodically review these assets for indicators of a limited useful life.&#160;&#160;The customer relationships for our FIGI&#8217;S business have been amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful life of four years and were fully amortized as of the end of Fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We test our goodwill and our indefinite-lived intangible assets for impairment at least annually or more frequently if there is an indication of possible impairment.&#160;&#160;We perform our annual impairment analysis during the fourth quarter of our fiscal year because our fourth quarter results of operations are significant to us and are an integral part of our analyses.&#160;&#160;In addition, we prepare our financial plan for the following fiscal year, which is an important part of our impairment analyses, during the fourth quarter of our fiscal year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our impairment test for goodwill involves a two-step process.&#160;&#160;The first step of the test involves comparing the fair values of the applicable reporting units with their aggregate carrying values, including goodwill.&#160;&#160;We determine the fair value of our reporting units using principally an income approach to valuation, which uses a discounted cash flow method to estimate the fair value of the reporting unit.&#160;&#160;If the carrying amount of a reporting unit exceeds the reporting unit&#8217;s fair value, we perform the second step of the goodwill impairment test to determine the amount of impairment loss.&#160;&#160;The second step of the goodwill impairment test involves comparing the implied fair value of the affected reporting unit&#8217;s goodwill with the carrying value of that goodwill.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Consistent with the methodology used to initially establish and record the fair value of the trademarks, we apply the &#8220;relief-from-royalty&#8221; method of the income approach in measuring the fair value of our tradenames for impairment testing.&#160;&#160;Under this method it is assumed that a company, without the rights to the trade names, would license the right to utilize them for business purposes.&#160;&#160;The fair value is estimated by discounting the hypothetical royalty payments to their present value over the estimated economic life of the asset.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We assigned the values of goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets recognized in connection with our acquisitions of LANE BRYANT, CATHERINES, Crosstown Traders, and FIGI&#8217;S to the respective reporting units within our reportable business segments.&#160;&#160;The calculation of the estimated fair value of our reporting units for the purpose of evaluating goodwill for impairment and the fair values of other intangible assets require estimates, assumptions, and judgments, and are &#8220;Level 3&#8221; fair value measurements (based on unobservable inputs that are not corroborated by market data).&#160;&#160;The results of our evaluations might have been materially different if different estimates, assumptions, and judgments had been used.&#160;&#160;Information on goodwill by business segment is included in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 5.&#160;&#160;INTANGIBLE ASSETS AND GOODWILL&#8221;</font> below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">See <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS&#8221; </font>and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 12. IMPAIRMENT OF STORE ASSETS, GOODWILL, AND TRADEMARKS&#8221;</font> below for further details regarding the recognition of impairment losses related to our goodwill and other intangible assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Asset Securitization</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Prior to the sale of our proprietary credit card receivables programs (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 11. SALE OF PROPRIETARY CREDIT CARD RECEIVABLES PROGRAMS&#8221;</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>below) we accounted for these programs as asset securitizations.&#160;&#160;Asset securitization primarily involved the sale of proprietary credit card receivables to a separate and distinct special-purpose entity, which in turn transferred the receivables to a separate and distinct qualified special-purpose entity (&#8220;QSPE&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The QSPE&#8217;s assets and liabilities were not consolidated in our balance sheets and the receivables transferred to the QSPE were isolated for purposes of the securitization program.&#160;&#160;The QSPE issued asset-backed certificates that represented undivided interests in those credit card receivables transferred into the QSPE.&#160;&#160;These certificates were sold to investors and we retained any undivided interests that remained unsold.&#160;&#160;We included these remaining undivided interests and any other retained interests in &#8220;Investment in asset-backed securities&#8221; in our accompanying consolidated balance sheets.&#160;&#160;The carrying value of these retained interests approximated their fair value.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We initially measured servicing assets and liabilities recognized in connection with our asset securitizations at fair value using a &#8220;Level 3&#8221; fair value measurement (based on unobservable inputs that are not corroborated by market data).&#160;&#160;Subsequent to initial recognition of the servicing assets or liabilities, we amortized the servicing assets or liabilities in proportion to, and over the period of, estimated net servicing income or loss and assessed the assets or liabilities for impairment or increased obligation based on fair value at each reporting date.&#160;&#160;See <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 16.&#160;&#160;ASSET SECURITIZATION&#8221;</font> below for further details regarding recognition and measurement of our servicing assets and liabilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Transaction expenses related to securitizations were deferred and amortized over the reinvestment period of the transaction.&#160;&#160;Net securitization income, including revaluation of our interest-only strip, was included as a reduction of selling, general, and administrative expenses in our accompanying consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Insurance Liabilities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We use a combination of third-party insurance and/or self-insurance for certain risks, including workers&#8217; compensation, medical, dental, automobile, and general liability claims.&#160;&#160;Our insurance liabilities are a component of &#8220;Accrued expenses&#8221; in our consolidated balance sheets and represent an estimate of the ultimate cost of uninsured claims incurred as of the balance sheet date.&#160;&#160;In estimating our self-insurance liabilities we use estimates of expected losses, which are based on analyses of historical data.&#160;&#160;Loss estimates are adjusted based upon actual claim settlements and reported claims.&#160;&#160;We evaluate the adequacy of these liabilities on a regular basis, modifying our assumptions as necessary, updating our records of historical experience, and adjusting our liabilities as appropriate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Senior Convertible Notes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.7pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We account for our 1.125% Senior Convertible Notes (the &#8220;1.125% Notes&#8221;) as cash-settled convertible securities, which are separated into their debt and equity components.&#160;&#160;The value assigned to the debt component is the estimated fair value, as of the issuance date, of a similar debt instrument without the conversion feature.&#160;&#160;As a result, the debt is recorded at a discount to adjust its below-market coupon interest rate to the market coupon interest rate for a similar debt instrument without the conversion feature.&#160;&#160;The difference between the proceeds for the convertible debt and the amount reflected as the debt component represents the value of the conversion feature and is recorded as additional paid-in capital.&#160;&#160;The debt is subsequently accreted to its par value over its expected life with an offsetting non-cash increase in interest expense on the income statement to reflect interest expense at the market rate for the debt component at the date of issuance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Concurrent with the issuance of the 1.125% Notes we entered into privately negotiated common stock call options and warrants with affiliates of the initial purchasers.&#160;&#160;We accounted for the call options and warrants as equity instruments and included the cost of the call options and the proceeds from the sale of the warrants in additional paid-in capital in our consolidated balance sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 1.125% Notes will have no impact on our diluted net income per share until the price of our common stock exceeds the conversion price.&#160;&#160;Prior to conversion we will include any dilutive effect of the 1.125% Notes or the warrants in the calculation of diluted net income per share using the treasury stock method.&#160;&#160;The call options are excluded from the calculation of diluted net income per share because their effect would be anti-dilutive.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.7pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We monitor the 1.125% Notes, call options, and warrants for compliance with the requirements for recognizing them as equity instruments on a quarterly basis.&#160;&#160;Should the issuance of the 1.125% Notes, the purchase of the call options, or the sale of the warrants fail to continue to qualify for treatment as equity instruments, we would be required to recognize derivative instruments in connection with the transactions, include the effects of the transactions in assets or liabilities instead of equity, and recognize changes in the fair values of the assets or liabilities in consolidated net income as they occur until the requirements for treatment as equity instruments are again met.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Revenue Recognition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Revenues from merchandise sales are net of discounts, returns and allowances, and coupons, and exclude sales tax.&#160;&#160;We record a reserve for estimated future sales returns based on an analysis of actual returns received, and we defer recognition of layaway sales to the date of delivery.&#160;&#160;Revenues from sales of gift cards are recorded as deferred revenue and recognized upon the redemption of the gift cards.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Catalog and e-commerce revenues include shipping and handling fees billed to customers.&#160;&#160;These revenues are recognized after the following have occurred: execution of the customer&#8217;s order, authorization of the customer&#8217;s credit card has been received, and the product has been shipped to and received by the customer.&#160;&#160;We record a reserve for estimated future sales returns based on an analysis of actual returns.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We sell gift cards to our Retail Stores segment customers through our stores, retail-store-related websites, and through third parties.&#160;&#160;We recognize revenue from gift cards when the gift card is redeemed by the customer.&#160;&#160;Our gift cards do not contain expiration dates or inactivity fees.&#160;&#160;We recognize gift card breakage (unused gift card balances for which we believe the likelihood of redemption is remote) as net sales based on an analysis of historical redemption patterns.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Loyalty Card Programs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We offer our customers various loyalty card programs (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 10.&#160;&#160;CUSTOMER LOYALTY CARD PROGRAMS</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221;</font> below).&#160;&#160;Customers that join these programs are entitled to various benefits, including discounts on purchases, during the membership period.&#160;&#160;Customers join some of these programs by paying an annual membership fee.&#160;&#160;For these programs we recognize revenue as a component of net sales over the life of the membership period based on when the customer earns the benefits and when the fee is no longer refundable.&#160;&#160;Certain loyalty card customers earn points for purchases which may be redeemed for merchandise coupons upon the accumulation of a specified number of points.&#160;&#160;No membership fees are charged in connection with these programs.&#160;We recognize an accrual for discounts earned and not yet issued and discounts issued but not yet redeemed based on an analysis of historical redemption patterns.&#160;&#160;Costs we incur in connection with administering these programs are recognized in selling, general, and administrative expenses as incurred.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Cost of Goods Sold</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Cost of goods sold includes merchandise costs net of discounts and allowances, freight, inventory shrinkage, and shipping and handling costs associated with our catalog and e-commerce businesses.&#160;&#160;We capitalize net merchandise costs and freight as inventory costs.&#160;&#160;Cost of goods sold also includes certain costs incurred in connection with our customer loyalty card programs (see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Loyalty Card Programs&#8221;</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>above) and the costs of producing and distributing our merchandise catalogs (see <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Deferred and Non-Deferred Advertising Costs&#8221;</font> above).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Occupancy and Buying Expenses</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Occupancy expenses include rent; real estate taxes; insurance; common area maintenance; utilities; maintenance; and depreciation for our stores, warehouse and fulfillment center facilities, and equipment.&#160;&#160;Buying expenses include payroll; payroll-related costs; and operating expenses for our buying departments and distribution centers.&#160;&#160;Occupancy and buying expenses are treated as period costs and are not capitalized as part of inventory.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Stock-based Compensation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Current grants of stock-based compensation consist primarily of stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;) and restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;).&#160;&#160;We use the Black-Scholes valuation model to estimate the fair value of stock options and SARs.&#160;&#160;We amortize stock-based compensation on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period of an award except for awards that include a market condition, which are amortized on a graded vesting basis over their derived service period.&#160;&#160;The Black-Scholes model requires estimates or assumptions as to the dividend yield and price volatility of the underlying stock, the expected life of the option, and a relevant risk-free interest rate, which are more fully described in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 9. STOCK-BASED COMPENSATION PLANS&#8221;</font> below.&#160;&#160;Stock-based compensation for performance-based awards is initially determined using an estimate of performance levels expected to be achieved and is periodically reviewed and adjusted as required.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2009 and Fiscal 2008 we also granted cash-settled RSUs under our 2003 Non-Employee Directors Compensation Plan.&#160;&#160;We record stock-based compensation related to cash-settled RSUs as a liability and adjust the liability and related compensation expense for changes in the market value of our common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We present gross excess tax benefits related to stock-based compensation as cash flows from financing activities in our statements of cash flows and we reflect write-offs of deferred tax assets related to an excess of stock-based compensation recognized in the financial statements over amounts deductible for tax purposes as cash flows used by operating activities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Costs Associated With Exit or Disposal Activities</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recognize liabilities for costs associated with exit or disposal activities when the liabilities are incurred and value the liabilities at fair value.&#160;&#160;One-time benefit payments are recognized as employees render service over future periods if the benefit arrangement requires employees to render future service beyond a minimum retention period.&#160;&#160;We record severance payments that are offered in accordance with an on-going benefit arrangement no later than the period when it becomes probable that the costs will be incurred and the costs are reasonably estimable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Income Taxes</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recognize a tax benefit for a tax position that is more-likely-than-not to be sustained upon examination, based solely on its technical merits.&#160;&#160;We measure the recognized benefit as the largest amount that is more-likely-than-not to be realized on ultimate settlement, based on a cumulative probability basis.&#160;&#160;We record interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in income tax expense.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">For tax positions that initially fail to qualify for recognition, we recognize a benefit in the first interim period in which the position meets the &#8221;more-likely-than-not&#8221; threshold or is resolved through negotiation, litigation, or upon expiration of the statute of limitations.&#160;&#160;We subsequently de-recognize a previously recognized tax benefit if we subsequently determine that the tax position no longer meets the &#8220;more-likely-than-not&#8221; threshold of being sustained.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We consider a tax position to be &#8220;effectively settled&#8221; upon completion of an examination by a taxing authority without being legally extinguished.&#160;&#160;For tax positions considered effectively settled we recognize the full amount of the tax benefit, even if (1) the tax position is not considered more-likely-than-not to be sustained solely on the basis of its technical merits, and (2) the statute of limitations remains open.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recognize deferred tax assets for temporary differences that will result in deductible amounts in future years and for net operating loss and credit carryforwards.&#160;&#160;We recognize a valuation allowance against our deferred tax assets if, based on existing facts and circumstances, it is more-likely-than-not that some portion or all of the deferred tax assets will not be realized and we adjust the allowance for changes in our estimate of the portion of deferred tax assets that are more-likely-than-not to be realized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We permanently reinvest undistributed profits from our international operations and therefore have not provided for incremental United States income taxes on such undistributed profits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Net Income/(Loss) Per Share</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Net income/(loss) per share is based on the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during each fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Common shares that we hold as treasury stock are excluded from the computation of net income/(loss) per share.&#160;&#160;Net income per share assuming dilution is based on the weighted-average number of common shares and share equivalents outstanding.&#160;&#160;Common share equivalents include the effect of dilutive stock options, SARs, and stock awards, using the treasury stock method.&#160;&#160;Share equivalents are not included in the weighted-average shares outstanding for determining net loss per share, as the result would be anti-dilutive.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our 1.125% Notes do not impact our diluted net income per share unless the price of our common stock exceeds the conversion price of $15.379 per share because we expect to settle the principal amount of the 1.125% Notes in cash upon conversion.&#160;&#160;Our call options are not included in the calculation of diluted net income per share because their effect would be anti-dilutive.&#160;&#160;Should the price of our common stock exceed $21.607 per share we would include the dilutive effect of the additional potential shares that may be issued related to our warrants, using the treasury stock method.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Comprehensive Income</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The consolidated statements of operations and comprehensive income include transactions from non-owner sources that affect stockholders&#8217; equity.&#160;&#160;Unrealized gains and losses recognized in comprehensive income are reclassified to net income upon their realization.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Deferred Debt Acquisition Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Debt acquisition costs other than costs related to the equity component of our 1.125% Notes are deferred and amortized to interest expense on a straight-line basis over the life of the related debt agreement.&#160;&#160;Debt acquisition costs related to the equity component of our 1.125% Notes have been recognized as a reduction of additional paid-in capital (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 7.&#160;&#160;LONG-TERM DEBT&#8221;</font> below).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Costs of Computer Software Developed or Obtained for Internal Use</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Costs related to the development of internal-use software, other than those incurred during the application development stage, are expensed as incurred.&#160;&#160;Costs incurred during the application development stage are capitalized and amortized over the estimated useful life of the software.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Impact of Recent Accounting Pronouncements</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In January 2010 the FASB issued ASU 2010-06, <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#8220;Fair Value Measurements and Disclosures (Topic 820): Improving Disclosures about Fair Value Measurements.&#8221;</font>&#160;&#160;ASU 2010-06 describes amendments that require some new disclosures and clarifies certain existing disclosures about fair value measurements as set forth in ASC 820-10.&#160;&#160;These amendments, which were effective for annual and interim periods as of the beginning of Fiscal 2010, did not have a material impact on our financial position or results of operations.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On April 25, 2008 we began to explore a broad range of operating and strategic alternatives for our Crosstown Traders non-core misses apparel catalog titles in order to provide a greater focus on our core brands and to enhance shareholder value.&#160;&#160;The Crosstown Traders apparel catalog operations met the requirements to be accounted for as held for sale.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, the assets, liabilities, and results of operations of the Crosstown Traders apparel catalogs were reported as discontinued operations in our consolidated financial statements for Fiscal 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On August 25, 2008 we announced that we had entered into a definitive agreement to sell the Crosstown Traders non-core misses apparel catalogs to an affiliate of Orchard Brands, a portfolio company owned by Golden Gate Capital.&#160;&#160;The sale was completed on September 18, 2008.&#160;&#160;Crosstown Traders&#8217; apparel catalog operations and cash flows have been eliminated from our financial statements as of the date of sale and we did not have any significant involvement in the operations after the sale.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As part of the definitive agreement we retained certain components of the infrastructure of the Crosstown Traders apparel catalogs.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we entered into transitional service agreements with an affiliate of Orchard Brands to provide certain services, including information technology, use of existing facilities, and financial services.&#160;&#160;These services were to be provided for specified time periods ranging up to one year from the date of the agreement, depending on the services provided.&#160;&#160;In addition, an affiliate of Orchard Brands agreed to provide certain transitional services to us, including distribution and call center services, for specified time periods ranging up to one year from the date of the agreement.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to the transitional period, which ended during the third quarter of Fiscal 2009, we were responsible for the remaining lease liabilities for the retained facilities.&#160;&#160;We discontinued using the fixed assets related to the retained facilities after the transitional period and fully depreciated them over the transitional services period.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">At the time of the sale we evaluated the impact of the retained cash flows with regards to the transitional service agreements.&#160;&#160;We determined that the cash inflows and outflows over the transitional period were not expected to be significant and that the reporting of discontinued operations was therefore deemed appropriate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CHARMING SHOPPES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<br>
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The decrease in income tax receivables during Fiscal 2010 was principally a result of the receipt of Federal tax refunds that related primarily to our four-year NOL carryback for Fiscal 2008, which was made possible by H.R. 3548, the &#8220;Worker, Homeownership, and Business Assistance Act of 2009&#8221; (the &#8220;Act&#8221;), as well as the filing of an amended return.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Act, signed into law on November 6, 2009, contained a number of tax law changes, including a provision that permits companies to carry back applicable 2008 or 2009 NOLs up to five years, instead of the general two-year carryback.&#160;&#160;We recognized the tax effects of the Act, including the re-measurement of existing current and deferred tax assets and liabilities, as well as related valuation allowances, in the interim period that includes the enactment date of the change.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, during the Fiscal 2009 Fourth Quarter we reclassified our Fiscal 2008 NOL carryforward from deferred tax assets to income tax receivable, reduced the valuation allowance previously established for these NOLs, and recognized an income tax benefit of $29,461,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2008 we evaluated our assumptions regarding the recoverability of our deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;Based on all available evidence we determined that the recoverability of our deferred tax assets was more-likely-than-not limited to our available tax loss carrybacks.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we recognized a non-cash provision of $42,681,000 in continuing operations and $18,861,000 in discontinued operations to establish a valuation allowance against our net deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2010 and Fiscal 2009 we continued to have a valuation allowance established against our net deferred tax assets.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, during Fiscal 2010 we increased our valuation allowance and recognized a non-cash provision of $23,327,000 in continuing operations, and during Fiscal 2009 we increased our valuation allowance and recognized a non-cash provision of $13,481,000 in continuing operations, net of the above benefit resulting from the carryback of our remaining Fiscal 2008 NOLs.&#160;&#160;In future periods we will continue to recognize a valuation allowance until such time as the certainty of future tax benefits can be reasonably assured.&#160;&#160;When our results demonstrate a pattern of future profitability the valuation allowance may be adjusted, which would result in the reinstatement of all or a part of the net deferred tax assets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of January 29, 2011 we have U.S. Federal net operating loss carryforwards of $101,445,000 and state net operating loss carryforwards of $98,516,000 that are available to offset future U.S. Federal and state taxable income.&#160;&#160;The U.S. Federal net operating loss has a twenty-year carryforward period, with $34,544,000 expiring in 2029 and $66,901,000 expiring in 2030.&#160;&#160;The state net operating losses have carryforward periods of five to twenty years, with varying expiration dates and amounts as follows:&#160;&#160;$13,941,000 in one to five years, $24,167,000 in six to ten years, $16,421,000 in eleven to fifteen years, and $43,987,000 in sixteen to twenty years.&#160;&#160;There are other state net operating losses not included in the above amounts that have not been valued as a result of our certainty that they will not be realized in the future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our U.S. Federal income tax returns for Fiscal 2004 and beyond remain subject to examination by the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (&#8220;IRS&#8221;) due to statute of limitations and the filing of amended returns and NOL carryback claims.&#160;&#160;We file returns in numerous state jurisdictions, with varying statutes of limitations.&#160;&#160;Our state tax returns for Fiscal 2006 and subsequent years, depending upon the jurisdiction, generally remain subject to examination.&#160;&#160;The statute of limitations on a limited number of returns for years prior to Fiscal 2006 has been extended by agreement between us and the particular state jurisdiction.&#160;&#160;The earliest year still subject to examination by state tax authorities is Fiscal 2003.</font></div>

<td nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="TEXT-ALIGN: left; PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160;</font></td>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2007 we issued $275,000,000 in aggregate principal amount of 1.125% Senior Convertible Notes due May 1, 2014 (the &#8220;1.125% Notes&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The 1.125% Notes will mature on May 1, 2014 unless earlier repurchased by us or converted.&#160;&#160;As of January 29, 2011 we had an aggregate total of $1,215,000 of unamortized underwriting fees and transaction costs, which are included in &#8220;Other assets&#8221; on our condensed consolidated balance sheets and are being amortized to interest expense on an effective interest rate basis over the life of the notes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Holders of the 1.125% Notes may convert their notes based on a conversion rate of 65.0233 shares of our common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes (the equivalent of $15.379 per share), subject to adjustment upon certain events, only under the following circumstances as more fully described in the Indenture for the 1.125% Notes (the &#8220;Indenture&#8221;): (i) during specified periods, if the price of our common stock reaches specified thresholds; (ii) if the trading price of the 1.125% Notes is below a specified threshold; (iii) at any time after November 15, 2013; or (iv) upon the occurrence of certain corporate transactions.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
