<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Upon conversion we intend to deliver an amount in cash equal to the lesser of the aggregate principal amount of notes to be converted or our total conversion obligation.&#160;&#160;If our conversion obligation exceeds the aggregate principal amount of the 1.125% Notes we will deliver shares of our common stock in respect of the excess.&#160;&#160;However, we have the option, subject to the approval of our Board of Directors, to elect to satisfy our conversion obligation entirely in shares of our common stock.&#160;&#160;In connection with a &#8220;Fundamental Change&#8221; as defined in the Indenture, we also will deliver upon conversion of the notes additional shares of common stock as described in the Indenture.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition, upon a change in control, liquidation, dissolution, or de-listing of our common stock before maturity of the 1.125% Notes (each of which would constitute a &#8220;Fundamental Change&#8221; as defined in the Indenture), we may be required to repurchase for cash all or a portion of the 1.125% Notes for 100% of the principal amount of the notes plus accrued and unpaid interest, if any, up to but excluding the date of purchase.&#160;&#160;As of January 29, 2011 none of the conditions allowing holders of the 1.125% Notes to convert or to require us to repurchase the 1.125% Notes had been met.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Concurrent with the issuance of the 1.125% Notes we entered into privately negotiated common stock call options with affiliates of the initial purchasers.&#160;&#160;The call options allowed us to purchase up to 17,881,000 shares of our common stock at an initial strike price of $15.379 per share.&#160;&#160;The call options expire on May 1, 2014 and must be net-share settled.&#160;&#160;The cost of the call options was $90,475,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition, we sold warrants to affiliates of certain of the initial purchasers that gave them the option to purchase up to 18,775,000 shares of our common stock at an initial strike price of $21.607 per share.&#160;&#160;The warrants expire on various dates from July 30, 2014 through December 18, 2014 and must be net-share settled.&#160;&#160;We received $53,955,000 in cash proceeds from the sale of these warrants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The call options and warrants are intended to reduce the potential dilution to our common stock upon conversion of the 1.125% Notes by effectively increasing the initial conversion price of the notes to $21.607 per share, representing a 73% conversion premium over the closing price of $12.49 per share for our common stock on April 30, 2007.&#160;&#160;We used a portion of the net proceeds from the 1.125% Notes to pay the $36,520,000 net cost of the call options and warrants.&#160;&#160;The cost of the call options and the proceeds from the sale of the warrants are included in additional paid-in capital in our accompanying condensed consolidated balance sheets.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2010 we repurchased $49,185,000 aggregate principal amount of 1.125% Notes with $10,094,000 of unamortized discount for a purchase price of $38,260,000 and recognized a gain of $1,907,000 net of unamortized issue costs.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2009 we repurchased $85,364,000 aggregate principal amount of 1.125% Notes with $20,923,000 of unamortized discount for a purchase price of $50,633,000 and recognized a gain of $13,979,000 net of unamortized issue costs.&#160;&#160;Approximately $1,584,000 of the Fiscal 2010 aggregate purchase price and $1,256,000 of the Fiscal 2009 aggregate purchase price was accounted for as a reduction of stockholders&#8217; equity.&#160;&#160;In conjunction with the repurchases we unwound a portion of our positions in the call options and warrants that we had purchased and sold in Fiscal 2007 to hedge the impact of the convertible debt (see above), which had an immaterial impact on our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 1.125% Notes will have no impact on our diluted net income per share until the price of our common stock exceeds the conversion price of $15.379 per share because the principal amount of the 1.125% Notes will be settled in cash upon conversion.&#160;&#160;Prior to conversion we will include the effect of the additional shares that may be issued if our common stock price exceeds $15.379 per share using the treasury stock method.&#160;&#160;For the first $1.00 by which the price of our common stock exceeds $15.379 per share there would be dilution of approximately 558,000 shares.&#160;&#160;Further increases in the share price would result in additional dilution at a declining rate, such that a price of $21.607 per share would result in cumulative dilution of approximately 2,633,000 shares.&#160;&#160;Should the stock price exceed $21.607 per share we would also include the dilutive effect of the additional potential shares that may be issued related to the warrants using the treasury stock method.&#160;&#160;The 1.125% Notes and warrants would have a combined dilutive effect such that, for the first $1.00 by which the stock price exceeds $21.607 per share, there would be cumulative dilution of approximately 3,346,000 shares prior to conversion.&#160;&#160;Further increases in the share price would result in additional dilution at a declining rate.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The call options are not included in the calculation of diluted net income per share because their effect would be anti-dilutive.&#160;&#160;Upon conversion of the 1.125% Notes the call options will serve to neutralize the dilutive effect of the notes up to a stock price of $21.607 per share.&#160;&#160;For the first $1.00 by which the stock price exceeds $21.607 per share the call options would reduce the cumulative dilution of approximately 3,346,000 shares in the example above to approximately 425,000 shares.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The preceding calculations assume that the average price of our common stock exceeds the respective conversion prices during the period for which diluted net income per share is calculated and exclude any potential adjustments to the conversion ratio provided under the terms of the 1.125% Notes.&#160;&#160;The calculations include the impact of our repurchases of a portion of the 1.125% Notes (see above).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Inasmuch as our 1.125% Notes are cash-settled convertible securities, they are separated into their debt and equity components (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 1.&#160;&#160;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES; </font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Senior Convertible Notes&#8221;</font> above).&#160;&#160;Upon maturity of the 1.125% Notes we will be obligated to repay to holders of the notes the principal value of the notes outstanding as of January 29, 2011 less the principal value of any additional notes that we repurchase prior to maturity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have a loan and security agreement (the &#8220;Agreement&#8221;) for a $225,000,000 senior secured revolving credit facility that provides for committed revolving credit availability through July 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;The amount of credit available from time to time under the Agreement is determined as a percentage of the value of eligible inventory, accounts receivable, and cash, as reduced by certain reserves.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Agreement includes an option allowing us to increase our credit facility up to $300,000,000, based on certain terms and conditions.&#160;&#160;The credit facility may be used for general corporate purposes, and provides that up to $100,000,000 of the $225,000,000 may be used for letters of credit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Agreement provides for borrowings under either &#8220;Base Rate&#8221; loans or &#8220;Eurodollar Rate&#8221; loans.&#160;&#160;Borrowings under Base Rate loans will generally accrue interest at a margin ranging from 2.75% to 3.25% over the Base Rate (as defined in the agreement) and Eurodollar Rate loans will generally accrue interest at a margin ranging from 3.75% to 4.25% over the London Interbank Offered Rate (&#8220;LIBOR&#8221;).&#160;&#160;As of January 29, 2011 the applicable rates under the facility were 6.00% (Base Rate plus 2.75%) for Base Rate Loans and 4.01% (LIBOR plus 3.75%) for Eurodollar Rate Loans.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The Agreement provides for customary representations and warranties and affirmative covenants.&#160;&#160;The Agreement also contains customary negative covenants providing limitations, subject to negotiated exceptions, for sales of assets; encumbrances; indebtedness; loans, advances and investments; acquisitions; guarantees; new subsidiaries; dividends and redemptions; transactions with affiliates; changes in business; limitations or restrictions affecting subsidiaries; credit card agreements; proprietary credit cards; and changes in control of certain of our subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;At any time during which &#8220;Excess Availability&#8221; (as defined in the Agreement) is less than $40,000,000 we will be required to maintain a minimum fixed charge coverage ratio of at least 1.1 to 1 for the then preceding twelve-month fiscal period.&#160;&#160;The Agreement also provides for certain rights and remedies if there is an occurrence of one or more events of default under the terms of the Agreement.&#160;&#160;Under certain conditions the maximum amount available under the Agreement may be reduced or terminated by the lenders and the obligation to repay amounts outstanding under the Agreement may be accelerated.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In connection with the Agreement we executed an Amended and Restated Guaranty (the &#8220;Amended Guaranty&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Pursuant to the Amended Guaranty, we and most of our subsidiaries jointly and severally guaranteed the borrowings and obligations under the Agreement, subject to standard insolvency limitations.&#160;&#160;Under the Amended Guaranty, collateral for the borrowings under the Agreement consists of pledges by us and certain of our subsidiaries of the capital stock of each such entity&#8217;s subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;The Agreement also provides for a security interest in substantially all of our assets excluding, among other things, equipment, real property, and stock or other equity and assets of excluded subsidiaries.&#160;&#160;Excluded subsidiaries are not Guarantors under the Agreement and the Amended Guaranty.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of January 29, 2011 we had an aggregate total of $3,687,000 of unamortized deferred debt acquisition costs related to the facility that will be amortized on a straight-line basis over the life of the facility as interest expense.&#160;&#160;There were no borrowings outstanding under the facility as of January 29, 2011.&#160;&#160;As of January 29, 2011, we were not in violation of any of the covenants included in the facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2008 we acquired $5,959,000 of distribution center, technology, and office equipment under capital leases.&#160;&#160;These capital leases generally have initial terms ranging from 36 months to 72 months and contain a bargain purchase option.&#160;&#160;As of January 29, 2011 the imputed interest rates on our outstanding capital leases ranged from 2.28% to 6.30%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Repayment of the 6.07% mortgage note is based on a 15-year amortization schedule, with 119 monthly installments of principal and interest of $110,000 and a balloon payment of $5,923,000 in October 2014.&#160;&#160;The note may be prepaid upon the payment of a premium or, upon certain other events, without the payment of a premium.&#160;&#160;The note is secured by a mortgage on real property at our distribution center in Greencastle, Indiana and an Assignment of Lease and Rents and Security Agreement related to the Greencastle facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 6.53% mortgage note has a ten-year term with 120 monthly installments of principal of $117,000 plus interest.&#160;&#160;The note is secured by a mortgage on land, a building, and certain fixtures we own at our distribution center in White Marsh, Maryland.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 7.77% mortgage note has a ten-year term with 119 monthly installments of principal and interest of $103,000 and a balloon payment of $5,220,000 in December 2011.&#160;&#160;The note is secured by a mortgage on land, buildings, and fixtures we own at our offices in Bensalem, Pennsylvania and by leases we own or rents we receive, if any, from tenants of the Bensalem facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2010 Stock Award and Incentive Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On April 28, 2010 our Board of Directors approved, and on June 24, 2010 our shareholders approved, our 2010 Stock Award and Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2010 Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The 2010 Plan replaces our 2004 Stock Award and Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2004 Plan&#8221;) and no new awards will be granted under the 2004 Plan.&#160;&#160;Shares for equity awards to our non-employee directors under our 2003 Non-Employee Directors Compensation Plan (the &#8220;2003 Plan&#8221;), including grants of awards in Fiscal 2010, will also be drawn from the 2010 Plan and no further awards will be granted from remaining shares which were reserved under the 2003 Plan.&#160;&#160;In addition, no further awards will be granted under our 1988 Key Employee Stock Option Plan (the &#8220;1988 Plan&#8221;).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The number of shares reserved for issuance under the 2010 Plan consist of 4,000,000 shares plus (i) 2,414,004 shares remaining available under the 2004 Plan, which have been transferred to the 2010 plan, and (ii) shares subject to outstanding awards under the 2004 Plan and predecessor plans (2000 Associates&#8217; Stock Incentive Plan, 1999 Associates&#8217; Stock Incentive Plan, and 1993 Employees&#8217; Stock Incentive Plan) that are canceled, forfeited, or otherwise become available under the share recapture provisions of the 2010 Plan.&#160;&#160;Unissued shares remaining available under the 2003 Plan and 1988 Plan as of June 24, 2010 will not be added to the shares authorized under the 2010 Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 2010 Plan provides for a broad range of awards, including stock options; stock appreciation rights (&#8220;SARs&#8221;); restricted stock units (&#8220;RSUs&#8221;); restricted stock awards (&#8220;RSAs&#8221;); deferred stock; other stock-based awards; dividend equivalents; performance shares or other stock-based performance awards; cash-based performance awards; and shares issuable in lieu of rights to cash compensation.&#160;&#160;Stock options include both incentive stock options and non-qualified stock options.&#160;&#160;Executive officers and other employees of Charming Shoppes, Inc. and its subsidiaries, non-employee directors, consultants, and others who provide substantial services to us are eligible for awards under the 2010 Plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 2010 Plan includes a limitation on the amount of awards that may be granted to any one participant in a given fiscal year in order to qualify awards as &#8220;performance-based&#8221; compensation not subject to the limitation on deductibility under Section 162(m) of the Internal Revenue Code.&#160;&#160;The 2010 Plan does not allow the amendment or replacement of options or SARs previously granted under the 2010 Plan in a transaction that constitutes a &#8220;re-pricing&#8221; under generally accepted accounting principles without shareholder approval and does not authorize loans to participants.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2004 Stock Award and Incentive Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our 2004 Plan was approved by our Board of Directors and our shareholders in Fiscal 2004.&#160;&#160;In 2009 our shareholders re-approved the material terms of the performance goals under the 2004 Plan in order to preserve our Federal income tax deduction for performance-based awards under the plan.&#160;&#160;This plan replaced our 1993 Employees&#8217; Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;1993 Plan&#8221;), our 1999 Associates&#8217; Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;1999 Plan&#8221;), and our 2000 Associates&#8217; Stock Incentive Plan (the &#8220;2000 Plan&#8221;), which are described below.&#160;&#160;As a result of the adoption of our 2010 Plan (see above), no further awards will be granted under this plan.&#160;&#160;The plan was administered by our Board of Directors and its Compensation Committee.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The 2004 Plan provided for the grant of options (including both incentive and non-qualified stock options), RSAs, SARs, RSUs, and a variety of other types of awards.&#160;&#160;Awards representing an aggregate of up to 6,500,000 shares of our common stock, together with shares remaining available under the 1993 Plan and shares recaptured from outstanding awards under the 1993 Plan, 1999 Plan, and 2000 Plan, could be issued under this plan.&#160;&#160;Of the aggregate shares available, up to 2,000,000 shares could be issued in connection with &#8220;full-value&#8221; awards (equity awards for which a participant does not pay at least the grant-date fair market value of the award, such as RSAs or RSUs).&#160;&#160;Additional shares could be used for full-value awards by reducing the number of shares that remained available for options, SARs, and other non-full-value awards by three shares for each share to be used for full-value awards in excess of the 2,000,000 share limit.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The aggregate number of shares subject to awards granted under the 2004 Plan in any fiscal year could not exceed 2% of our common stock on a fully diluted basis as of the last day of the preceding fiscal year.&#160;&#160;The 2004 Plan prohibits the amendment or replacement of options or SARs granted under the plan in a transaction that constitutes a &#8220;re-pricing&#8221; under generally accepted accounting principles without shareholder approval.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">2003 Non-Employee Directors Compensation Plan</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our 2003 Plan was approved by shareholders in Fiscal 2003.&#160;&#160;Directors who are not employed by our company are eligible to participate in the plan.&#160;&#160;Our Board of Directors administers the plan and approves the form and amount of awards under the plan.&#160;&#160;This plan provided for the grant of stock options, SARs, RSAs, RSUs, or deferred shares of up to an aggregate total of 600,000 shares of our common stock.&#160;&#160;No more than 50% of the shares reserved for issuance under the plan could be issued as restricted stock awards or RSUs.&#160;&#160;As a result of the adoption of the 2010 Plan (see above), shares for equity awards to our non-employee directors under the 2003 Plan, including grants of awards in Fiscal 2010, will also be drawn from the 2010 Plan and no further awards will be granted from remaining shares which were reserved under the 2003 Plan.&#160;&#160;The 2003 Plan is a sub-plan under the 2010 Plan and represents the policy-governing directors&#8217; compensation, which is subject to modification or replacement from time to time by the Board of Directors.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Under the 2003 Plan annual RSUs for a number of shares equivalent to $135,000 of aggregate market value on the date of grant were granted to each non-employee director serving at the date of our Annual Meeting of Shareholders.&#160;&#160;Each RSU represents a right to receive one share of common stock or cash of equal value, at the company&#8217;s option, at the date of vesting or, if deferred by the director, at a later date after termination of service.&#160;&#160;Non-employee directors could also elect to receive deferred shares of common stock of an equivalent market value instead of cash director&#8217;s fees.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The exercise price of options or SARs granted under the 2003 Plan could not be less than the fair market value of our common stock on the date of grant.&#160;&#160;The maximum term of options and SARs issued under the plan is ten years.&#160;&#160;The plan includes a provision that options previously granted under the plan will not be amended or replaced in a transaction that constitutes a &#8220;re-pricing&#8221; as defined in the plan without shareholder approval.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 10.&#160;&#160;CUSTOMER LOYALTY CARD PROGRAMS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We offer our customers various loyalty card programs.&#160;&#160;Customers that join these programs are entitled to various benefits, including discounts on purchases, during the membership period.&#160;&#160;Customers join some of these programs by paying an annual membership fee.&#160;&#160;For these programs we recognize revenue as a component of net sales over the life of the membership period based on when the customer earns the benefits and when the fee is no longer refundable.&#160;&#160;We recognize costs we incur in connection with administering these programs as selling, general, and administrative expenses when incurred.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our FASHION BUG brand offers a customer loyalty card program that we operate under our FASHION BUG private-label credit card program.&#160;&#160;Like our other loyalty programs, this program entitles customers to various discounts and other benefits upon payment of an annual membership fee.&#160;&#160;The program provides customers with the option to cancel their membership within 30 days, entitling them to a full refund of their annual fee.&#160;&#160;The FASHION BUG brand also offers a loyalty card program that does not charge membership fees.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our CATHERINES brand offers a loyalty card program that entitles customers to various discounts and other benefits upon payment of an annual membership fee.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our LANE BRYANT brand offers a loyalty program in connection the LANE BRYANT proprietary credit card.&#160;&#160;Cardholders earn points for purchases using the credit card, which may be redeemed for merchandise coupons upon the accumulation of a specified number of points.&#160;&#160;No membership fees are charged in connection with this program.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">CHARMING SHOPPES, INC. AND SUBSIDIARIES</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 11.&#160;&#160;SALE OF PROPRIETARY CREDIT CARD RECEIVABLES PROGRAMS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In Fiscal 2009 we sold our proprietary credit card receivables programs to World Financial Network National Bank (&#8220;WFNNB&#8221;), a subsidiary of Alliance Data Systems Corporation (&#8220;Alliance Data&#8221;), and entered into ten-year operating agreements (the &#8220;operating agreements&#8221;) with Alliance Data for the provision of private-label credit card programs for our customers.&#160;&#160;We received net cash proceeds of $136,647,000 related to the transaction and recognized one-time net charges as a result of the sale of $14,237,000, primarily related to contract termination, transaction, severance, and retention costs.&#160;&#160;Further information regarding our proprietary credit card receivables programs is included in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 16.&#160;&#160;ASSET SECURITIZATION&#8221;</font> below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The transaction consisted of the sale of our proprietary credit card portfolio, along with certain other assets and liabilities that are required to support these card programs, including our consolidated balance sheet asset &#8220;Investment in asset-backed securities.&#8221;&#160;&#160;The components of the investment in asset-backed securities comprising the net sales proceeds were $51,250,000 of outstanding trust certificates owned by Charming Shoppes Receivables Corp. (&#8220;CSRC&#8221;), $60,922,000 of cash account balances in the Charming Shoppes Master Trust (the &#8220;Trust&#8221;) that had been funded by CSRC, an interest-only strip of $21,714,000, and other retained interests of $2,761,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Gross proceeds from the transaction were $166,647,000.&#160;&#160;Approximately $30,000,000 of the gross proceeds was used to fund the termination of contractual obligations related to the transaction as well as exit costs.&#160;&#160;In addition, on the sale date, we surrendered the charter of the Spirit of America National Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), our wholly-owned credit card bank, and merged the remaining assets and liabilities of the Bank into another non-banking subsidiary.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We receive ongoing payments from Alliance Data under the operating agreements based on credit sales generated by our private-label credit card customers.&#160;&#160;These payments are recognized as a reduction of selling, general and administrative expenses, similar to revenues associated with our proprietary credit card receivables program prior to the sale.&#160;&#160;Alliance Data assumed the servicing obligations for the Trust, which was renamed the World Financial Network Credit Card Trust II, effective as of the date of sale.&#160;&#160;Therefore, we have no further obligations with respect to financing our credit card programs.&#160;&#160;The operating agreements may be terminated early by either party for cause upon the occurrence of certain events as specified in the agreements including, but not limited to: unsatisfactory performance by WFNNB under the terms of the agreements; substantial declines in private-label credit card sales volume or substantial closings of sales channels; and events of insolvency or other material defaults.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 12.&#160;&#160;IMPAIRMENT OF STORE ASSETS, GOODWILL, AND TRADEMARKS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During Fiscal 2010 we performed an impairment review of long-lived assets and identified 157 stores with asset carrying values in excess of such stores&#8217; respective forecasted undiscounted cash flows.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2009 we performed an impairment review of long-lived assets and identified 89 stores with asset carrying values in excess of such stores&#8217; respective forecasted undiscounted cash flows.&#160;&#160;During Fiscal 2008 we identified 272 stores with asset carrying values in excess of such stores&#8217; respective forecasted undiscounted cash flows.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we recognized non-cash impairment charges to write down the long-lived assets (primarily leasehold improvements) at these stores to their respective fair values.&#160;&#160;Due to the nature of the assets being written down (primarily leasehold improvements) and our past history of abandoning such assets, we have determined the fair value of the assets to be minimal.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As a result of the significant decrease in the market value of our common stock during the third quarter of Fiscal 2008 and the impact of the then-current economic environment on our results of operations,<font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline">&#160;</font>we performed a review of our goodwill and other intangible assets with indefinite lives for possible impairment.&#160;&#160;Based on our assessment we determined that our goodwill and other indefinite-lived intangible assets were not impaired as of the third quarter of Fiscal 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2008 we performed a goodwill impairment test for each of our reporting units that had recorded goodwill and indefinite-lived intangible assets (LANE BRYANT, CATHERINES, and FIGI&#8217;S).&#160;&#160;Based on that impairment test we determined that our CATHERINES goodwill was impaired.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we recognized a non-cash impairment charge related to the CATHERINES goodwill.&#160;&#160;In addition, we recognized a non-cash impairment charge as a result of our plans to discontinue the use of certain other acquired trademarks and tradenames.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The non-cash impairment charges recognized in connection with these write-downs were as follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fiscal 2010 Closure of Under-performing Stores</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the Fiscal 2010 Fourth Quarter we announced the planned closing of approximately 215 additional under-performing stores of which a majority are FASHION BUG stores.&#160;&#160;We expect to close 200 of these under-performing stores in Fiscal 2011.&#160;&#160;Included in the 215 under-performing store closures are 30 CATHERINES stores in outlet locations that did not meet our profitability objectives and therefore will be closed over a two year period.&#160;&#160;As a result of the decision to close the CATHERINES stores in outlet locations, we recognized a non-cash impairment charge of $3,210,000.&#160;&#160;We expect to incur approximately $7,000,000 for lease termination and other costs primarily related to the closing of the CATHERINES stores in outlet locations over the next two years to complete the above closures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As a result of the resignation of our former chief executive officer during the Fiscal 2010 Third Quarter we recognized severance and related costs, including accelerated stock compensation costs, in accordance with the severance agreement.&#160;&#160;The liability as of January 29, 2011 represents the remaining severance obligation that is scheduled to be paid to him over the next two years.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fiscal 2009 Closure of Under-performing Stores</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the Fiscal 2009 Fourth Quarter we performed an impairment review of long-lived assets and identified 89 stores with asset carrying values in excess of such stores&#8217; respective forecasted undiscounted cash flows (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 12.&#160;&#160;IMPAIRMENT OF STORE ASSETS, GOODWILL, AND TRADEMARKS&#8221;</font> above).&#160;&#160;In conjunction with that review we announced a store closing program for approximately 40 &#8211; 50 of those impaired stores.&#160;&#160;As a result of the decision to close these stores we incurred lease termination charges and expect to close approximately 40 remaining stores by the end of Fiscal 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Closing of PETITE SOPHISTICATE OUTLET Stores</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">To further focus on our core brands, we closed our PETITE SOPHISTICATE OUTLET stores during Fiscal 2009 and converted a majority of the space to CATHERINES stores in outlet locations during Fiscal 2010.&#160;&#160;As a result of the decision to close and convert these stores, we recognized non-cash depreciation, lease termination costs, and other closure costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As part of the definitive agreement for the sale of the Crosstown Traders apparel catalogs (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS&#8221;</font> above), we retained certain components of the infrastructure of the Crosstown Traders apparel catalogs.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we entered into transitional service agreements with an affiliate of Orchard Brands (the purchaser) to provide certain services, including information technology, use of existing facilities, and financial services.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to the transitional period, which ended during the Fiscal 2009 Third Quarter, we were responsible for the remaining lease liabilities for the retained facilities.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we recognized non-cash accelerated depreciation related to the retained fixed assets over the transitional services period.&#160;&#160;We recognized a lease termination liability of approximately $11,141,000 as a result of the termination of the transitional service agreements when we ceased to use the retained leased facilities.&#160;&#160;The lease termination liability represents the present value of the remaining lease liability, less estimated sub-lease rental income, discounted using a credit-adjusted risk-free rate, and was initially recorded at fair value using a &#8220;Level 3&#8221; fair value measurement (based on unobservable inputs that are not corroborated by market data).</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Transformational Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We began to execute on a new multi-year strategy in Fiscal 2008 with the assistance of experienced third-party retail consultants to ensure the viability of the Company and our brands, enhance our competitive position, and to improve our financial results over time.&#160;&#160;The strategy encompassed refocusing on our core retail brands; simplifying the business by eliminating distractions and divesting non-core assets; substantially reducing operating expenses and streamlining operations; and maintaining and protecting our strong balance sheet and liquidity position.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Shutdown of LANE BRYANT WOMAN Catalog</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the Fiscal 2008 Third Quarter we decided to discontinue our LANE BRYANT WOMAN catalog.&#160;&#160;As a result of this decision we recognized a markdown allowance of $4,220,000, which is included in cost of goods sold in Fiscal 2008, to properly state inventory at the lower of cost or market.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we recognized severance and retention costs for the elimination of approximately 100 positions and non-cash accelerated depreciation related to fixed assets that we ceased to use after the closure of the catalog.&#160;&#160;We completed the shutdown of LANE BRYANT WOMAN catalog during the Fiscal 2009 Second Quarter.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fiscal 2008 Elimination of Positions</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In the Fiscal 2008 Third Quarter we announced a further workforce reduction of approximately 225 positions, which represented both terminations and elimination of open positions.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we recognized severance costs related to the terminated employees.&#160;&#160;We completed the payment of severance for the terminated employees in Fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fiscal 2008 Closure of Under-performing Stores</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In the Fiscal 2008 Fourth Quarter we announced a store closing program for approximately 100 under-performing stores.&#160;&#160;As a result of the decision to close these stores we incurred non-cash accelerated depreciation in Fiscal 2009. We completed the under-performing store closing program in Fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">figure Magazine Shutdown Costs</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In the Fiscal 2008 Fourth Quarter we decided to shutdown our <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">figure</font> magazine operation.&#160;&#160;As a result of this decision, we incurred contract termination costs in accordance with the terms of our third-party agreement.&#160;&#160;We completed the shutdown of the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">figure </font>magazine in the second quarter of Fiscal 2009.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 14.&#160;&#160;EMPLOYEE RETIREMENT BENEFIT PLANS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We provide a comprehensive retirement benefit program for our employees.&#160;&#160;The program includes a 401(k) employee savings plan under which eligible participating employees may elect to contribute up to 80% of their compensation to an investment trust.&#160;&#160;The 401(k) plan includes a provision for a matching company contribution of 50% of the participant&#8217;s elective contribution on up to 6% of the participant&#8217;s compensation.&#160;&#160;As of the beginning of April 2009 the matching company contribution for this plan was suspended, and no matching company contributions have been made to the plan through January 29, 2011.&#160;&#160;Participating employees are immediately vested in their own contributions.&#160;&#160;Full vesting in the matching company contribution occurs on the earlier of the participant&#8217;s attainment of 5 years of service or upon retirement, death, or disability, as defined in the plan.&#160;&#160;Company matching contributions are made in cash, and the available trust investment options do not include investment in our own common stock.&#160;&#160;The program also provides for a noncontributory profit-sharing plan that covers substantially all full-time employees who meet age and service requirements.&#160;&#160;Contributions to this plan are completely discretionary and are determined by our Board of Directors on an annual basis.&#160;&#160;There were no contributions to the profit-sharing plan during Fiscal 2010, Fiscal 2009, or Fiscal 2008.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We provide a non-qualified deferred compensation plan to officers and certain key executives.&#160;&#160;Under this plan participants may contribute up to 77% of their base compensation and 90% of bonus compensation.&#160;&#160;This plan includes a provision for a matching company contribution of 50% of the participant&#8217;s contribution on up to 6% of the participant&#8217;s compensation, less any matching contributions made for the participant under our 401(k) plan.&#160;&#160;As of the beginning of April 2009 the matching company contribution for this plan was suspended, and no matching company contributions have been made to the plan through January 29, 2011.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Through December 31, 2008 we also provided a non-qualified defined contribution supplemental retirement plan for certain management and key executives.&#160;&#160;Under this plan we contributed amounts to participant accounts based on age and years of plan service, as well as earnings as defined in the plan.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We discontinued the non-qualified defined contribution supplemental retirement plan effective as of December 31, 2008 and ceased making retirement credits to the plan.&#160;&#160;In addition, we reduced the interest rate to be credited on participants&#8217; accounts under the plan to 3.5% and participants&#8217; accounts became fully vested.&#160;&#160;Distribution of participant accounts occur over one-to-three years based on the account balance.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0.9pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Prior to the sale of our proprietary credit card receivables programs our FASHION BUG, LANE BRYANT, CATHERINES, and PETITE SOPHISTICATE proprietary credit card receivables were originated by Spirit of America National Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), our wholly-owned credit card bank.&#160;&#160;The Bank transferred its interest in all of the receivables associated with these programs to the Charming Shoppes Master Trust (the &#8220;Trust&#8221;) through Charming Shoppes Receivables Corp., a separate and distinct special-purpose entity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">On August 25, 2008 we announced that we entered into an agreement to sell our misses apparel catalog credit card receivables in connection with the sale of the related Crosstown Traders catalog titles (see <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;NOTE 2.&#160;&#160;DISCONTINUED OPERATIONS&#8221;</font> above).&#160;&#160;On December 31, 2008 we finalized the sale of the credit card receivables portfolio associated with the Crosstown Traders misses apparel catalogs to World Financial Network National Bank, a unit of Alliance Data Systems Corporation.&#160;&#160;The portfolio was sold for a par value of $43,526,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The sale of the Crosstown Traders portfolio enabled us to pay off and terminate a related conduit securitization facility that was dedicated to these receivables.&#160;&#160;The sale of the credit card receivables and the elimination of funding-related cash collateral requirements, less the prepayment of securitized indebtedness, resulted in net cash proceeds to us of $12,455,000.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Prior to the sale of our proprietary credit card receivables programs we accounted for the securitization of our proprietary credit card receivables as follows:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" width="100%" style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">
<tr>
<td valign="top" width="6%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -5.75pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#9679;</font></div>
</td>
<td valign="top" width="79%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The QSPEs sold interests in the receivables on a revolving basis for a specified term.&#160;&#160;At the end of the revolving period, an amortization period began during which the QSPEs made principal payments to the parties that entered into the securitization agreement with the QSPEs.&#160;&#160;All assets of the QSPEs (including the receivables) were isolated and supported the securities issued by those entities.</font></div>
</td>
</tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="6%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160; </font></td>
<td valign="top" width="79%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160; </font></td>
</tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="6%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -5.75pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#9679;</font></div>
</td>
<td valign="top" width="79%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We recorded gains or losses on the securitization of our proprietary credit card receivables based on the estimated fair value of the assets retained and liabilities incurred in the sale.&#160;&#160;Gains represented the present value of the estimated cash flows that we retained over the estimated outstanding period of the receivables.&#160;&#160;This excess cash flow essentially represented an I/O strip, consisting of the present value of the finance charges and late fees in excess of the amounts paid to certificate holders, credit losses, and servicing fees.</font></div>
</td>
</tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="6%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160; </font></td>
<td valign="top" width="79%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#160; </font></td>
</tr><tr>
<td valign="top" width="6%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -5.9pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#9679;</font></div>
</td>
<td valign="top" width="79%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We used various valuation assumptions in determining the fair value of our I/O strip.&#160;&#160;We estimated the values for these assumptions using historical data, the impact of the current economic environment on the performance of the receivables sold, and the impact of the potential volatility of the current market for similar instruments in assessing the fair value of the retained interests.</font></div>
</td>
</tr></table>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">YEAR ENDED JANUARY 29, 2011</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">(Continued)</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: -5.9pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">&#9679;</font></div>

<td valign="top" width="79%">
<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">In addition, we recognized a servicing liability because the servicing fees we expected to receive from the securitizations did not provide adequate compensation for servicing the receivables.&#160;&#160;The servicing liability represented the present value of the excess of our cost of servicing over the servicing fees received and was recorded at its estimated fair value.&#160;&#160;Because quoted market prices were generally not available for the servicing of proprietary credit card portfolios of comparable credit quality, we determined the fair value of the cost of servicing by calculating all costs associated with billing, collecting, maintaining, and providing customer service during the expected life of the securitized credit card receivable balances.&#160;&#160;We discounted the amount of these costs in excess of the servicing fees over the estimated life of the receivables sold.<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>The discount rate and estimated life assumptions used for the present value calculation of the servicing liability were consistent with those used for the I/O strip.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 18.&#160;&#160;SEGMENT REPORTING</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We operate and report in two segments: Retail Stores and Direct-to-Consumer.&#160;&#160;We determine our operating segments based on the way our chief operating decision-makers review our results of operations.&#160;&#160;We consider our retail stores and store-related e-commerce as operating segments that are similar in terms of economic characteristics, production processes, and operations.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we have aggregated our retail stores and store-related e-commerce into a single reporting segment (the &#8220;Retail Stores&#8221; segment).&#160;&#160;Our catalog and catalog-related e-commerce operations, excluding discontinued operations, are separately reported under the Direct-to-Consumer segment.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">The accounting policies of the segments are generally the same as those described in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">NOTE 1.&#160;&#160;SUMMARY OF SIGNIFICANT ACCOUNTING POLICIES</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8221; </font>above.&#160;&#160;Our chief operating decision-makers evaluate the performance of our operating segments based on a measure of their contribution to operations, which consists of net sales less the cost of merchandise sold and certain directly identifiable and allocable operating costs.&#160;&#160;We do not allocate certain corporate costs, such as shared services, information systems support, and insurance to our Retail Stores or Direct-to-Consumer segments.&#160;&#160;Operating costs for our Retail Stores segment consist primarily of store selling, buying, occupancy, and warehousing.&#160;&#160;For our Direct-to-Consumer segment, operating costs consist primarily of catalog development, production, and circulation; e-commerce advertising; warehousing; and order processing.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Corporate and Other net sales consist primarily of revenue related to our <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">figure</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;</font>magazine, which we discontinued during Fiscal 2009.&#160;&#160;Corporate and Other operating costs include unallocated general and administrative expenses; shared services; insurance; information systems support; corporate depreciation and amortization; corporate occupancy; and other non-routine charges.&#160;&#160;Operating contribution for the Retail Stores and Direct-to-Consumer segments less Corporate and Other net expenses equals income before interest and income taxes.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="ControlsandProcedures"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>Item 9A.&#160;&#160;Controls and Procedures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be disclosed in reports we file under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, is recorded, processed, summarized, and reported within the time periods specified in the Securities and Exchange Commission&#8217;s rules and forms, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to our management, including our Chief Executive Officer (&#8220;CEO&#8221;) and Chief Financial Officer (&#8220;CFO&#8221;), as appropriate and in such a manner as to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure.&#160;&#160;Our Disclosure Committee, which is made up of several key management employees and reports directly to the CEO and CFO, assists our management, including our CEO and CFO, in fulfilling their responsibilities for establishing and maintaining such controls and procedures and providing accurate, timely, and complete disclosure.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">As of the end of the period covered by this report on Form 10-K (the &#8220;Evaluation Date&#8221;), our Disclosure Committee, under the supervision and with the participation of management, including our CEO and CFO, carried out an evaluation of the effectiveness of the design and operation of our disclosure controls and procedures.&#160;&#160;Based on this evaluation, our management, including our CEO and CFO, has concluded that, as of the Evaluation Date, our disclosure controls and procedures were effective.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Evaluation of Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Management&#8217;s Report on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting as of January 29, 2011 appears on page 67 of this Report on Form 10-K, and is incorporated herein by reference.&#160;&#160;The Report of our Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm on Internal Control Over Financial Reporting appears on pages 68 - 69 of this Report on Form 10-K, and is incorporated herein by reference.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Changes in Internal Control Over Financial Reporting</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Except for the following, there has been no change in our internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the fiscal quarter ended January 29, 2011 that has materially affected, or is reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">During the fourth quarter of Fiscal 2010 we implemented a new human resources platform, including payroll, which is hosted by a third-party provider.&#160;&#160;In conjunction with the implementation we modified the design, operation, and documentation of our internal control over financial reporting.&#160;&#160;Specifically, we modified controls in the business processes impacted by the new system, such as user access security, system reporting and authorization, and reconciliation procedures.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><a name="DirectorsandOfficers"><!--EFPlaceholder--></a>Item 10.&#160;&#160;Directors, Executive Officers, and Corporate Governance</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Information regarding our directors and executive officers is included under the captions <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;DIRECTORS STANDING FOR ELECTION,&#8221;</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;BIOGRAPHIES OF DIRECTORS AND NOMINEES FOR DIRECTOR,&#8221;</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AT CHARMING SHOPPES,&#8221;</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;COMPENSATION OF DIRECTORS,&#8221;</font> AND <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;SECTION 16(A) BENEFICIAL OWNERSHIP REPORTING COMPLIANCE&#8221;</font> in our definitive proxy statement to be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission within 120 days of the end of our fiscal year, which is incorporated herein by reference.&#160;&#160;Information regarding Executive Officers is included under <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Additional Part I Information &#8211; Our Executive Officers,&#8221;</font> in Part I of this Report.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">We have adopted the Charming Shoppes, Inc. Business Ethics and Standards of Conduct Policy (the &#8220;Policy&#8221;) that applies to all of our directors, officers, and associates, including our principal executive officer, principal financial officer, and principal accounting officer.&#160;&#160;The Policy has been filed as Exhibit 14 to this report on Form 10-K.&#160;&#160;We have also adopted the Charming Shoppes, Inc. Complete Principles of Corporate Governance (the &#8220;Principles&#8221;) and charters (the &#8220;Charters&#8221;) for the audit committee, the compensation committee, and the corporate governance and nominating committee of our Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;The Policy, Principles, and Charters are available on our internet website, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">www.charmingshoppes.com</font>, in the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;About Us&#8221;</font> section, under <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#8220;Corporate Governance&#8221;</font>.&#160;&#160;A copy of the Policy, Principles, and Charters are also available, at no charge, upon written request to Charming Shoppes, Inc., Attn. Director of Investor Relations, 3750 State Road, Bensalem, PA, 19020.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 40pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; FONT-SIZE: 12pt">Our Board of Directors has sole authority for making any amendments to, or granting waivers from, any provision of the Policy that affects our executive officers or directors, including our principal executive officer, principal financial officer, or principal accounting officer.&#160;&#160;We intend to satisfy the disclosure requirement under Item 5.05 of Form 8-K regarding any such amendment or waiver by disclosing the nature of such amendment or waiver in a report on Form 8-K within four days.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block"><br>
